H4102.fullDef: H4102. mahah [ מָהַהּ ] verb only Hithpalpel linger, tarry (compare Arabic slow walk, delay ( †am. )); — Hithpalpel Perfect 1singular הִתְמַהְמָ֑הְתִּי Psa 119:60 ; 3 plural הִתְמַהְמְהוּ Judg 19:8 ; 1 plural הִתְמַהְמָ֑הְנוּ Gen 43:10 ; Imperfect יִתְמַהְמַהּ Hab 2:3 ; ׳וַיִּתְמ Gen 19:16 ; Imperative masculine plural הִתְמַהְמְהוּ Isa 29:9 ; Infinitive לְהִתְמַחְמֵהַּ Exod 12:39 ; Participle מִתְמַהְמֵהַּ 2Sam 15:28 ; — linger, tarry, wait , of person, Gen 19:16 ; 43:10 (J), Exod 12:39 (E), Judg 3:26 ; 19:8 ; 2Sam 15:28 ; Isa 29:9 ; Psa 119:60 (with לֹא , opposed to חַ֫שְׁתִּי ); subject חָזוֺן vision Hab 2:3 מְהוּמָה see הום . מְהוּמָן see אמן . מְהֵיטַבְאֵל see יטב .

H4103.fullDef: H4103. mehumah מְהוּמָה noun feminine tumult, confusion, disquietde, discomfiture — absolute ׳מ Deut 7:23 7 t.; construct מְהוּמַת 1Sam 5:11 ; Ezek 22:5 ; plural absolute מְהוּמוֺת 2Chr 15:5 , מְהוּמֹת Amos 3:9 ; — 1 tumult, confusion Amos 3:9 (|| עֲשׁוּקִים oppression ), disturbance, turmoil (opposed to peace) 2Chr 15:5 (|| verb המם 15:6 ), compare Ezek 22:5 ; disquietude (of mind) Prov 15:16 ; especially tumult & confusion, panic , as due to divine judgment ׳מְהוּמַתיֿ Zech 14:13 compare Ezek 7:7 ; also 1Sam 5:9 and מָוֶת מְהוּמַת 5:11 . 2 discomfiture , (due to ׳י ) in war 1Sam 14:20 (compare 14:15 ; 14:22 ); Deut 7:23 (accusative of congnate meaning with verb with הום q. v.), 28:20 (|| מִגְעֶרֶת מְאֵרָה, ); compare מ ׳יוֺם 1Sam 22:5 (|| מְבוּכָה מְבוּסָה, ) a day of discomfiture & down-treading & confusion .

Aralli , compare Len Origines ii, ch. ix ). 3 appointed place: a. the temple, || שׂכּוֺ Lam 2:6 , ממ ׳נוּגֵי afflicted (and driven) from the place of assembly Zeph 3:18 (compare Br MP 225 ). b. synagogues, בָּאָרֶץ כָּלמֿוֺעֲדֵיאֵֿל all the appointed places of El in the land Psa 74:8 = וַעַד בֵּית Sota 9:15 . 4 appointed sign, signal , Judg 20:38 . 5 מוֺעֵד אֹהֶל tent of meeting (of God with his people: see יָעַד Niph`al 1 ); the sacred tent of the Exodus (see אֹהֶל 3 ) Exod 33:7 (twice in verse); Num 12:4 ; Deut 31:14 (twice in verse) (E), Num 11:16 (J); often in P, as Exod 27:21 ; 29:4 ; Lev 1:1 , 3 ; Josh 18:1 ; 19:51 , etc. (131 t.)>; elsewhere only 1Sam 2:22 b (omitted by ᵐ5 ), 1Kin 8:4 2Chr 5:5 ; 1Chr 6:17 ; 9:21 ; 23:32 ; 2Chr 1:3 , 6 , 13 .

H4161.fullDef: H4161. motsa I. מוֺצָא noun masculine Hosea 6:3 place or act of going forth, issue, export, souce, spring ; — absolute ׳מ Job 28:1 ; Psa 75:7 ; construct ׳מ Num 30:13 9 t.; מֹצָא Job 38:27 ; Dan 9:25 ; suffix מוֺצָאֲךָ 2Sam 3:25 ; מֹצָאוֺ Hosea 6:3 ; מוֺצָאוֺ Psa 19:7 ; plural construct מוֺצָאֵי Isa 41:18 5 t.; suffix מוֺצָאָיו Ezek 43:11 ; מוֺצָאֵיהֶם Num 33:2 (twice in verse); מוֺצָאֵיהֶן Ezek 42:11 ; — 1 a going forth: a. the act, of ׳י Hosea 6:3 ; of the sun = rising Psa 19:7 (see יצא 1f ); of man 2Sam 3:25 (opposed to מָבוֺא Kt); ׳מ דָּבָר Dan 9:25 going forth of a command. b. concrete , גּוֺלָה מוֺצָאֵי Ezek 12:4 goings forth of exile, i.e. those going forth into exile (in simile). c. way out, exit: concrete, of chambers in temple Ezek 42:11 ; 43:11 (opposed to מוֺבָאָיו ); הַמִּקְדָּשׁ מוֺצָאֵי 44:5 (opposed to הַבַּיִת מְבוֺא ). 2 that which goes forth: a. utteranc of mouth or lips (especially of solemn or formal speech), פִייֿ ׳מוֺצָא Deut 8:3 ; מ ׳שְׂפָתַי Jer 17:16 ; Psa 89:35 ; so Deut 23:24 ; Num 30:13 (P). b. export of horses 1Kin 10:23 2Chr 1:16 . 3 place of going forth: a. source or spring of water 2Kin 2:21 ; Isa 58:11 (in simile) Psa 107:33 (|| נְהָרוֺת ), 107:35 (|| אֲגַםמֿים ) = Isa 41:18 (|| id. ); הָעֶלְיוֺן גִיחוֺן מֵימֵי מוֺצָא 2Chr 32:30 . b. place of departure of Israel on marchNum 2Chr 33:2 (twice in verse) (P). c. מוֺצָא = east (place of sun's going forth) Psa 75:7 (opposed to מַעֲרָב ); zeugmatically, 65:9 וָעֶרֶב בֹּקֶר מוֺצָאֵי i.e. the east and the west (compare the two Orients , Qor 43:37). d. place whence silver comes = mine Job 28:1 ; דֶשֶׁא מֹצָא וּלְהַצְמִיחַ 38:27 and to cause the growing-place (others, the growth ) of young grass to sprout.

H4196.fullDef: H4196. mizbeach מִזְבֵּחַ 401 noun masculine Josh 22:10 altar (Arabic , place of slaughter, trench made by torrent , Sabean מדֿבח DHM Epigr. Denkm. 24 ); ׳מ absolute 2Kin 18:22 223t., הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה Exod 29:13 31 t.; construct מִזְבַּח 20:24 76t., suffix מִזְבְּחִי 20:26 7 t., מִזְבַּחֲךָ 1Kin 8:31 3 t., מִזְבְּחֶ֑ךָ Deut 33:10 ; מִזְבְּחוֺ Judg 6:31 2 t.; plural מִזְבְּחֹת Num 23:1 5 t., מִזְבְּחוֺת 2Kin 21:3 23 t., suffix מִזְבְּחוֺתֶיךָ Psa 84:4 , other suffixes 21 t.; — 1 J E narrate that altars were built by Noah after leaving the ark Gen 8:20 ; by Abraham at Shechem 12:7 , Bethel 12:8 , Hebron 13:18 , mountain in land Moriah 22:9 ; by Issac at Beersheba 26:25 ; by Jacob at Shechem 33:20 (yet this perhaps mistake for מַצֵּבָה , being object of וַיַּצֶּבשָֿׁם , not elsewhere with מזבח , compare also Di), at Bethel 35:7 , by Moses at Rephidim Exod 17:15 , Horeb 24:4 , by Balak at Bamoth Baal, Pisgah, & Peor Num 23:1 , 14 , 29 ; by Joshua on Mt. Ebal Josh 8:30 : the prophetic histories narrate that altars were built by Gideon at Ophra Judg 6:24 ; by a man of God at Bethel 21:4 ; by Samuel at Ramah 1Sam 7:17 ; by Saul after Michmash 14:35 ; by David on the threshing floor of Ornan 2Sam 24:25 = 1Chr 21:18 ; 22:1 ; that Solomon sacrificed on the altar at Gibeon 1Kin 3:4 and built altars in the temple at Jerusalem 6:20 ; 8:64 ; that Jeroboam built an altar at Bethel 12:32 (which was destroyed by Josiah 2Kin 23:15 ); and that Elijah repaired an ancient altar on Carmel 1Kin 18:30 . An altar in Egypt is predicted Isa 19:19 . All this accords with the law of the Covenant code Exod 20:24-26 which recognises a plurality of altars and prescribes that they shall be built of אֲדָמָה , or of unhewn stones, and without steps. So אֲבָנִים Deut 27:6 (JE), שְׁלֵמוֺת אֲבָנִים Josh 8:31 , and twelve stones 1Kin 18:30 , 32 ; compare Isa 27:9 . The altar was also a place of refuge Exod 21:24 (JE) 1Kin 1:50-51 , 2:28 . 2 D prescribes one central altar Deut 12:5 f. 27; but no attempt to enforce this principle appears before Hezekiah( 2Kin 18:4 , 22 ), and Josiah, whose reform is more effectual, 23:8-20 . 3 P limits sacrifices to the altars of the tabernacle . A great altar was built east of the Jordan, but it was according to P only as an עֵד after the pattern of the altar before the Tabernacle Josh 22:10-34 . P describes two altars: a. the הָעֹלָה מִזְבַּח Exod 30:28 ; 31:9 ; 35:16 ; 38:1 ; 40:6 , 10 , 29 ; Lev 4:7 , 10 , 25 (twice in verse); 4:30 , 34 = ׳מ הַנְּחשֶׁת Exod 38:30 ; 39:39 , made of acacia wood plated with brass, 5*5*3 cubits in size, with four horns and a network of brass, on which all sacrifices by fire were made 27:1 ; Exodus 8; 38:1-7 ; b. ׳מ קְטֹרֶת מִקְטַר made of acacia wood plated with gold, 1*1*2 cubits in size, with four horns and a crown of gold Exod 30:1-6 = ׳מ הקטרת 30:27 ; 31:8 ; 35:15 ; 37:25 = ׳מ הזהב 39:38 ; 40:5 , 26 ; Num 4:11 = ׳מ הַסַּמִּים קטרת Lev 4:7 ; these altars are named elsewhere only in Chronicles: 1Chr 6:34 ; 16:40 ; 21:29 ; 2Chr 1:5-6 ,. 4 Solomon made two altars for the temple at Jerusalem : a. ׳מ הַנְּחשֶׁת for the court 1Kin 8:64 (which was laid aside by Ahaz 2Kin 16:14-15 , who made an altar after the model of one he saw in Damascus 16:11 ); in 16:14 הַנּ ׳הַמִּזְבַּח (construct form with article) is erroneous, read probably מִזְבַּח compare Ges § 127 . 4 a near the end; this altar, according to Chronicles, measured 20*20*10 cubits 2Chr 4:1 ; this (ה)נחשׁת מזבח also 7:7 & Ezek 9:2 ; = ׳מ העולה 2Chr 29:18 , repaired by Asa 15:8 ; b. an altar of cedar, plated with gold, in the temple before the דְּבִיר 1Kin 6:20 , 22 ; 7:48 ; = ׳מ הזהב 2Chr 4:19 ; = ׳מ הַקְּטֹרֶת 1Chr 28:18 ; 2Chr 26:16 . 5 Ezekiel plans two altars for the new temple : a. a table of wood 3*2 cubits Ezek 41:22 ; b. an altar for the court , probably same dimensions as 4a , with stairs Ezek 43:13-17 . 6 after the return Jeshua built an altar on the ancient site in the court of the temple Ezra 3:2 . 7 besides these altars used in the worship of Yahweh, Ahab built an altar to Baal in Samaria 1Kin 16:32 ; Ahaz made an altar on the roof of the upper chamber, and other kings of Judah made altars in the two courts, all of which were destroyed by Josiah 2Kin 23:12 . 8 the ancient and most common term for making altars was בָּנָה Gen 35:7 (E) 8:20 (J) Deut 27:5-6 , Exod 32:5 (JE) +, implying building material; other verbs are הֵקִים 2Sam 24:18 ; 1Kin 16:32 ; 2Kin 21:3 ; 1Chr 21:18 ; 2Chr 33:3 ; הֵכִין Ezra 3:3 (followed by עַלמְֿכוֺנֹתָו֯ ); שִׂים Jer 11:13 ; וַיַּצֶּבֿ Gen 33:20 (but compare 1 ); Num 23:4 (E) has עָרַךְ arrange , prepare ; עָשָׂה Gen 35:1 , 3 ; Exod 20:24 (E) Gen 13:4 (J) Judg 22:28; 1Kin 12:33 ; 18:26 ; this becomes usual in P, Exod 27:1 ; 30:1 ; 37:25 ; 38:1 , 30 , Songs 2Chr 4:1 , 19 ; 7:7 ; 28:24 . 9 the dedication of the altar was המזבח חֲנֻכַּת Num 7:10-11 , 84 , 88 ; 2Chr 7:9 ; it was anointed with oil מָשַׁח Exod 40:10 ; Lev 8:11 ; Num 7:10 (all P). 10 removal of unlawful altars is expressed by נָתַץ Exod 34:13 (JE) Deut 7:5 ; Judg 2:2 ; 6:30-31 , 32 ; 2Kin 11:18 ; 23:12 , 15 ; נִתַּץ (Pi) Deut 12:3 ; 2Chr 31:1 ; 34:4 , 7 ; נֻתַּץ Judg 6:28 ; הָרַס 6:25 ; 1Kin 19:10 , 14 ; שִׁבַּר 2Chr 23:17 >; הֵסִיר 2Kin 18:22 = Isa 36:7 ; 2Chr 14:2 ; 30:14 ; 32:12 ; 33:15 . 11 ministry at the altar was הַמּ ׳מִשְׁמֶרֶת Num 18:5 ; Ezek 40:46 , compare Num 3:31 (P), מ ׳מְשָֽׁרְתֵי Joel 1:13 ; עַל עָמַד is said of officiating priest 1Kin 13:1 , עַל עָלָה Exod 20:26 ; 1Sam 2:28 ; 1Kin 12:33 + (compare יָרַד Lev 9:22 ); sacrifices were usually offered עַלהַֿמִּזְבֵּחַ Gen 22:9 ; Deut 12:27 +; see especially the phrases with זָרַק Exod 29:16 , 20 + (see זרק ); הִקְטִיר Lev 4:10 (see קטר Hiph`il ); הֶעֱלָה 6:3 + (see עלה Hiph`il ) לְבַעֵר Neh 10:35 ; but בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ Gen 8:20 (J) Num 23:2 , 4 , 14 , 30 (E); one touching the altar is בַּמּ ׳הַנֹּגֵעַ Exod 29:37 (P); המ ׳לפני of placing, or standing before altar Deut 26:4 ; 1Kin 8:22 ; as accusative of location הַמִּזְבֵּ֫חָה in phrases especially with הִקְטִיר Exod 29:13 +, and הֶעֱלָה Lev 14:20 . 12 the horns of the altar were especially for the application of the blood of the sin-offering in the ritual ; sin is represented as graven מִזְבְּחוֺתֵיכֶם לְקַרְנוֺת Jer 17:1 ; therefore of blood for cleansing it was said המ קרנות על ׳נָתַן Exod 29:12 ; Lev 4:7 , 18 , 25 , 30 , 34 ; 8:15 ; 9:9 ; 16:18 (all P). An ancient custom is referred to, Psa 118:27 המזבח עַדקֿרנות בַּעֲבֹתִ֑ים אִסְרוחַֿג bind the festal victim with cords, unto the horns of the altar: Ainsworth paraphrases: 'that is, all the court over, untill you come even to the hornes of the altar, intending hereby many sacrifices,' so De; but Che 'bind the procession with branches, (step on) to the altar-horns,' that is in sacred procession round the altar. 13 the יְסוֺד (q. v.) is also referred to in the ritual of the sin-offerings in the phrases יסוד אל יָצַק Lev 8:15 ; 9:9 & יסוד אל שָׁפַךְ Exod 29:12 ; Lev 4:7 , 18 , 25 , 30 , 34 (all P) יסוד אל יִמָּצֵה 5:9 . 14 the altar was קָדָשִׁים קֹדֶשׁ Exod 29:37 ; 40:10 (P); but repeated sin-offerings were necessary to keep it pure and cleanse it from the pollution of the people in whose midst it was situated. This is expressed by חִטֵּא Lev 8:15 (P) Ezek 43:22 ; כִּמֶּר Lev 16:20 , 33 (P) Ezek 43:26 ; קִדַּשׁ Exod 29:44 ; 40:10 ; Lev 8:15 ; Num 7:1 (P); טִהַר 2Chr 29:18 . זַבַּי see below זבב .

H4279.fullDef: H4279. machar מָחָר 52 noun masculine , used often as adverb , tomorrow, in time to come (Aramaic מְחַר ; probably properly time in front , Kö ii. 263 , compare √, and Assyrian ma—ru , front , often of time, though always of former time, of old , Dl HWB 402 ); — 1 to-morrow (the day following the present day), a. as substantive Exod 16:23 לְי קֹדֶשׁ שַׁבַּת ׳שַׁבָּתוֺן מָחָר to-morrow is a sabbath, etc., 1Sam 20:5 מָחָר חֹדֶשׁ to-morrow is the new moon, 20:18 ; in מָחָר יוֺם Gen 30:33 ; Prov 27:1 ; Isa 56:12 ; in the idiomatic phrase מָחָר כָּעֵת at the like of the time, (being) to-morrow, = about to-morrow (see כְּ 1a ) Exod 9:18 ; 1Sam 9:16 ; 20:12 ; 1Kin 19:2 ; 20:6 ; 2Kin 7:1 , 18 ; 10:6 ; and in לְמָחָר Exod 8:19 הַזֶּה הָאֹת יִהְיֶה לְמָחָר , = for, against, to-morrow , 8:6 ; Num 11:18 ; Josh 7:13 ; Est 5:12 . b. as adverb accusative Exod 8:25 ; 9:5 ׳י הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר יַעֲשֶׂה מָחָר , 10:4 אַרְבֶּה מָחָר מֵבִיא הִנְנִי , 17:9 ; 32:5 ; Num 14:25 ; 1Sam 11:9 etc., Josh 11:6 הַזּאֹת כָּעֵת מָחָר ; opposed to הַיּוֺם Exod 19:10 וּמָחָר הַיּוֺם , Josh 22:18 ; 2Sam 11:12 a; rhetorically, Isa 22:13 נָמוּת מָחָר כִּי . 2 = in future time , Exod 13:14 לֵאמֹר מָחָר בִנְךָ יִשְׁאָֽלְךָ כִּי = Deut 6:20 ; Josh 4:6 , 21 ; 22:24 , 27 , 28 ; so מָחָר בְּיוֺם Gen 30:33 .

H4310.definition: , Exod 32:26 לי ׳מי אלי who is on J
H4310.fullDef: H4310. mi מִי 423 pronoun interrogative who? of persons, as מָה (q. v.) of things (Ethiopic but only = What ? and How ? Assyrian mî, me (rare) Jäger BAS. ii. 277 , the usual Semitic form for Who? has n , namely Assyrian mannu, manu (Dl HWB 419 ), Ethiopic man¥ , Aramaic Arabic , Vulgar Arabic min, m£n , from a form resembling which, by rejection of n , probably Hebrew מִי : W SG 123 f. ): — who ? ( τίς ; quis ? ) Gen 3:11 מִי לְךָ הִגִּיד who told thee ? 24:65 הַלָּזֶה הָאִישׁ מִי who is this man ? 27:18 בני אתה מי who art thou, my son ? Num 22:9 ; Judg 1:1 ; 6:29 ; 15:6 ; 18:3 ; 20:18 ; 2Sam 1:8 + often; Ruth 3:9 אָ֑תְּ מִי who art thou, (feminine) ? Isa 51:12 ; of more than one, אֵלָּה מִי who are these ? Gen 33:5 ; 48:8 ; Isa 60:8 ; אתם מי 2Kin 10:13 ; once, more explicitly, הַהֹלְכִים זָמִי מִי Exod 10:8 ; = as who ? (i.e. in what condition, or capacity), Amos 7:2 יקום מי יעקב vAmos 7:5; Isa 51:19 אֲנַחֲמֵךְ מִי (but Vrss Che Lag Brd Du יְ ׳מִי , as || יָנוּד מִי ), Ruth 3:16 (Be Ke Kö iii. 388 ). Note in particular: a. מִי is rarely used of things , and usually where persons are understood or implied: Gen 33:8 הזה כלהֿמחנה לך מי who (or what ) to thee is all this camp ? Deut 4:7 ; Judg 9:28 מִי שְׁכֶם who is Shechem (i.e. the Shechemites) ? Micah 1:5 שֹׁמְרוֺן הֲלֹא יַעֲקֹב מִיפֶֿשַׁע , v b Song 3:6 ; Judg 13:17 שְׁמֶ֑ךָ מִי ( but מה Gen 32:28 ; Exod 3:13 : with מי compare מַן in Aramaic Ezra 5:4 ; Genesis, Exodus ll. cc. ᵑ7 ; and see Nö M. p. 341 ). On 1Sam 18:18 , see II. חַי b. in the Genitive, אַתְּ בַּתמִֿי whose daughter art thou ? Gen 24:23 , 47 ; 1Sam 12:3 (3 t. in verse); 17:55 ; Jer 44:28 ; Job 26:4 ; 33:28 ; after various prepositions, as מִי אַחֲרֵי 1Sam 24:15 (twice in verse); אֶלמִֿי 6:20 ; 2Kin 9:5 +; בְּמִי by whom ? 1Kin 20:14 , לְמִי 20 to whom ? whose ? Gen 32:18 אַתָּה לְמִי , 38:25 ; Prov 20:20 (6 t.) +; מִמִּי Ezek 32:19 ; Psa 27:1 (twice in verse); עַלמִֿי 2Kin 18:20 ; 19:22 ; Isa 57:4 +; אֶתמִֿי (so always in accusative), 1Sam 12:3 (twice in verse); 28:11 ; Isa 6:8 ; = with whom ? Job 12:3 . c. in an indirect question, as Gen 21:26 ; 43:22 שׂם מי ידענו לא we do not know who put , etc., Deut 21:1 ; Psa 39:7 ; Josh 24:15 תַעֲבֹד֑וּן אֶתמִֿי ֗֗֗ בַּחֲרוּ choose whom ye will serve, after ראה 1Sam 14:17 , שׁאל 17:56 , הגיד 1Kin 1:20 , הודיע 1:27 . d. ב ׳מי who among ... ? 1Sam 22:14 ; Isa 36:20 ; 43:9 ; 48:14 ( בהם ) 42:23 ; 50:10 ; Hag 2:3 ( all בכם ); מן מי who of ... ? Judg 21:8 ; 2Kin 6:11 ; Isa 50:1 . e. strengthened and emphatic forms of interrogative: ( a ) זה מי (see זה 4b ), הוא מי (see הוא 4b β ), מי זה הוא Psa 24:10 ; Jer 30:21 ; Est 7:5 (see ibid. ); ( b ) מִי אֶחָד what single one ... ? Judg 21:8 , compare 2Sam 7:23 ( = 1Chr 17:21 ). f. various rhetorical uses ( often repeated in || clause, as Psa 15:1 ; 18:32 ; Isa 28:9 ; 29:15 ): — (a) followed by imperfect it expresses a wish ( the question implying a desire that the person asked for were present ), 2Sam 15:4 שֹׁפֵט יְשִׂמֵנִי מִי who will set me judge ? i.e. would that some one would make me judge ! 23:15 מַיִם יַשְׁקֵנִי מִי = O that one would give me to drink, etc. ! compare Num 11:4 , 18 ; Mal 1:10 ; Psa 4:7 ; 60:11 ; 94:16 ; Isa 42:23 , and very often in the phrase יִתֵּן מִי who will give? i.e. would that there were. . . ! as Num 11:29 י עם כל יתן ׳ומי נביאים = and would that all ׳י s people were prophets! Deut 28:67 ערב יתן מי = would it were even! Judg 9:29 + (see נָתַן ). (b) it expresses contempt (who ? implying the answer no one at all ), Exod 5:2 י מי בקולו אשׁמע ׳אשׁר who is ׳י that I should listen to his voice ? Judg 9:28 נַעַבְדֶנּוּ כִּי שְׁכֶם וּמִי אֲבִימֶלֶךְ מִי , 9:38 ; 1Sam 17:26 who is this Philistine that he should have reproached, etc.? 25:10 ישׁי בן ומי דוד מי Isa 28:9 ; Job 26:4 ; Prov 30:9 י ׳מי ; or modesty (real or assumed), Exod 3:11 אֶלמַּֿרְעֹה אֵלֵךְ כִּי אָנֹכִי מִי 1Sam 18:18 אנכי מי חיי ומי who am I, and who is my clan ( חַיִּי ), that I should be the king's son-in-law ? 2Sam 7:18 ; 1Chr 29:14 ; 2Chr 2:5 ; or surprise , Isa 44:10 ; 49:21 . (c) in impassioned prose, and especially in poetry, implying the answer few or none , it is equivalent to a rhetorical negative, Deut 9:2 עֲנָק בְנֵי לִפְנֵי יִתְיַצֵּב מִי who can stand, etc.? 30:12 הַשָּׁמַיְמָה יַעֲלֶהלָּֿנוּ מִי 30:13 ; 1Sam 4:8 וג יַצִּילֵנוּ ׳מִי , 6:20 ; 22:14 ; 26:9 , 15 ; 2Sam 16:10 ; יאמר מי who shall (or can) say ? Job 9:12 ; Prov 20:9 ; Eccl 8:4 ; with the perfect (of experience), who has ever . . . ? Num 23:10 ; Deut 5:23 ; Isa 36:20 ; 66:8 (twice in verse); Jer 18:13 כָּאֵלֶּה שָׁמַע מִי , 23:18 ( ᵑ0 ), 30:21 ; Job 4:7 ; 9:4 וַיִּשְׁלָ֑ם אֵלָיו הִקְשָׁה מִי , 41:3 ; Prov 30:4 ; Lam 3:37 ; in poetry, very often, as Gen 49:9 וּכְלָבִיא יְקִימֶנּוּ מִי who can rouse him up ? (i.e. no one), Exod 15:11 (twice in verse) כָמוֺךָ מִי (so Psa 35:10 and elsewhere), Num 24:9 , 23 ; 1Sam 2:25 לו יתפלל מי who shall intercede for him ? (i.e. no one), Isa 1:12 ; 10:3 ; 40:13-14 , 18 ; 41:26 ; 42:19 ; 43:9 ; 48:14 ; 50:1 ; 53:1 לִשְׁמֻעָתֵנוּ הֶאֱמִין מִי (i.e. few or none), etc.; Psa 18:32 י מִבַּלְעֲדֵי אֱלוֺהַּ ׳מִי , 76:8 ; 89:7 ; 130:3 ; Job 21:31 ; 34:29 ; Jer 17:9 ; Joel 2:11 ; Mal 3:2 ; ֗֗֗ לֹא מִי Amos 3:8 ; Jer 10:7 ; Job 12:9 (compare 25:3 ; Nahum 3:19 ); ( יְשִׁיבֶנָּה ) יְשִׁיבֶנּוּ מִי who shall (can) turn it back ? Job 9:12 ; 11:10 ; 23:13 ; Isa 14:27 ; 43:13 ; Jer 2:24 ; implying the answer, no one but God , Isa 40:12 ; 41:2 ; Job 38:5 ; 35:6 ; Job 35:25, etc.; defiantly, Isa 50:9 יַרְשִׁיעֵנִי הוּא מִי , Jer 21:13 ; 49:4 אֵלַי יָבוֺא מִי , 49:19 ; Obadiah 3; Psa 12:5 לָנוּ אָדוֺן מִי , 59:8 ; 64:6 ; Job 9:19 לְמִשְׁמָּט וְאִם יוֺעִידֵנִי מִי , 13:19 עִמָּדִי יָרִיב הוּא מִי who is he that will contend with me ? 17:3 ; 41:2 . Notice in examples of this kind the frequent order of words: Prov 20:6 ימצא מי אמוּנים ואישׁ , 24:22 מי שׁניהם ופיד יודע , 31:10 ; Nahum 1:6 יעמד מי זעמו לפני , Psa 147:17 לפני יעמד מי קֹרָתוֺ , Job 4:2 יוּכ֑ל מִי בְּמִלִּין וַעְצֹר , 26:14 ; 38:37 ; 39:5 ; 41:5 ; 41:6 ; Psa 6:6 יוֺדֶהלָּֿ֑ךְ מִי בִּשְׁאוֺל , 19:13 ; and with the nom. pendens , Jer 2:24 יְשִׁיבֶנָּה מִי תַּאֲנָתָהּ , Prov 18:14 ; Job 17:15 יְשׁוּרֶנָּה מִי וְתִקְוָתִי , 38:29 יְלָדוֺ מִי שָׁמַיִם וּכְפֹר . ( d ) יוֺדֵעַ מִי who knoweth ? ( Psa 90:11 ; Prov 24:22 ), followed by a verbal clause, becomes (compare nescio an ) = it may be, perchance , 2Sam 12:22 י יְחָנֵּנִי יוֺדֵעַ ׳מִי (Qr וְחַנַּנִי ), Joel 2:14 ( = Jonah 3:9 ) ונחם ישׁוב יודע מי , Est 4:14 מי אם יודע . Job, and in לְמִנִּי Micah 7:12 (twice in verse) and מִנֵּיֿ (on analogue of עֲלֵי עֲדֵי, ) Isa 30:11 (twice in verse), preposition expressing the idea of separation , hence out of, from, on account of, off, on the side of, since, above, than, so that not (Phoenician מ ; Aramaic ; Arabic >; Ethiopic ; Sabean בן (DHM ZMG xxix.606 ff. ; xxxvii.375)); with suff, מִמֶּנִּי (the מִן reduplicated, Ol § 223c , and others, Kö ii. 289 f. ), in poetry מִנִּי 22:4 ; 30:1 ; 38:12 ; Job 16:6 , מֶ֫נִּי Psa 18:23 ; 65:4 ; 139:19 ; Job 21:16 ; 22:18 ; 30:10 ; מִמֵּךְ מִמֶּ֑ךָּ, מִמְּךָ, ; מִמֶּ֫נּוּ ( 4:12 מֶ֫נְהוּ ), מִמֶּ֫נָּה ; 1 plural מִמֶּ֫נּוּ (according to Orientals מִמֵּ֫נֿוּ : see Baer Job. p. 57 Kö 290 ); מִכֶּם ; מֵהֶם ( מִנְּהֶם 11:20 ), מֵהֵ֫מָּה Jer 10:2 ; Eccl 12:12 ; מֵהֵ֫נָּה 7t. (see הֵ֫מָּה 8c ), מֵהֶן (editions מֵהֵן ) Ezek 16:47 , 52 (see Zerweck Heb, Präp. Min, 1894 ): — 1. with verbs expressing (or implying) separation or removal , whether from a person or place, or in any direction, also from guilt, calamity, etc.: — thus a. to descend from a mountain Exod 19:14 , to fall from a roof Deut 22:8 , from heaven Isa 14:12 , to go up from a valley Josh 10:7 , to raise up from the dunghill 1Sam 2:8 , or the ground 2Sam 12:17 . So constantly with verbs of going , as ברח שׁב, הלך, בא, (followed by a person, usually מפני ), of calling , as Isa 24:14 מִיָּם צָֽהֲלוּ , 42:10-11 , Psa 148:1 of asking or exacting as נָקַם דרשׁ, בקשׁ, שׁאל, , הִנָּקֵם , of delivering , as הציל הושׁיע, , etc., of hiding as העלים נעלם, , etc., of taking or withholding , as מנע חשׂך, לקח, , of keeping ( from ), as שׁמר נצר, , of being far , or desisting , as רחק Exod 23:7 , מִמֶּנּוּ חֲדַל desist from us, 14:2 , so הֶרֶף Deut 9:14 , הֵנִיחַ 12:10 , השׁקיט > Psa 94:13 , שׁבת Gen 2:2 , compare 5:29 ; note especially the pregnant constructions, שׁפט to judge (and save) from Psa 43:1 , followed by מִיַּד 1Sam 24:16 +, ענה to answer (and save) from Psa 22:22 , חרשׁ and חשׁה to be silent (turning) from 28:1 (twice in verse), ממני החרישׁו Job 13:13 ; Jer 38:27 ; Psa 18:22 מאלהי רשׁעתי ולא not did wickedly (turning) from my God, 30:4 Kt., 73:27 , ממך כלזֿוֺנֶה , Jer 3:20 מִן בָּגַד ( ᵐ5 εἰς = ב ), 31:13 with שִׂמַּח ( 2Chr 20:27 ), Ezek 27:34 ; Prov 25:17 ; רֵעֶ֫ךָ מִבֵּית רַגְלְךָ הֹקַר , Isa 29:4 ; 63:17 ; Joel 1:12 ; Jer 51:5 מֵאֱלֹהָיו אַלְמָן widowed (and severed) from etc., Ezek 44:22 ; also Judg 7:17 תַּעֲשׂוּ וְכֵן תִרְאוּ מִמֶּנִּי ye shall see from me, i.e. learn what to do by observing me. Some of the verbs mentioned above are construed more precisely with מֵעַל מֵעִם, מֵאֵת, , q. v.: and others, especially מִּלֵּט מּדה, הצּיל, הושׁיע, דרשׁ, לקח, , idiomatic with מִיַּד . With infinitives, see below 7b. often also with adverbs, as מִשָּׁם thence , מֵאַיִן whence ? מִמֹּה מִוֶּה, hence . compare also מִן חָפְשִׁי free (safe) from Job 3:19 , מִצָּרָיו עֵזֶר a help from his foes Deut 33:7 ; Nahum 3:11 מֵאוֺיֵב מָעוֺז , Psa 32:7 מִצַּר סֵתֶר , Psalm 60:13 מִצָּ֑ר עֶזְרָת , Isa 4:6 מֵחֹרֶב צֵל a shadow from , the heat, 25:4 . Here also belong 40:15 מִדְּלִי מַר a drop from (hanging from) a bucket; Song 4:1 goats גלעד מהר שֶׁגָָּֽלְשׁוּ that sit up (seeming to hang) from the hills of Gilead (compare Od. 21. 420 ἐκ διφροιο καθήμενος : also the Arabic idiom , literally to be near from a thing): probably also the difficult passage Dan 8:9 , and from one of them there came forth אַחַת קֶרֶן מִצְּעִירָה a horn from (being) a little one, i.e. gradually increasing from small beginnings (but ? read צְעִירָה אַחֶרֶת Bev compare 7:8 ). b. מן also, without a verb of similar significance, sometimes expresses the idea of separation, away from, far from (compare II. 2. 162 φίλης ἀπὸ πατρίδος αἴης ): Prov 20:3 מֵרִיב שֶׁכֶת to sit away from strife (compare ap. De), Num 15:24 if the thing be done הָעֵדָה מֵעֵינֵי away from the eyes of etc., Judg 5:11 De RV (but Be RVm because of ), Isa 14:19 cast out מִקִּבְרְךָ away from thy sepulchre, Job 28:4 מֵאֱנוֺשׁ דַּלּוּ , Gen 4:11 cursed art thou מןֿ האדמה , De Di away from the (tilled) soil, compare 4:14 (but Kn Ke from , compare 4:12 a), 27:39 (probably) מִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ away from the fatness of the earth shall be thy dwelling; almost = without , Job 11:15 then shalt thou lift up thy face מִמּוּם away from, without spot, 19:26 (probably) מִבְּשָׂרִי without my flesh shall I see God, 21:9 מִמַּחַד שָׁלוֺם בָּֽתֵּיהֶם are at peace without fear, Prov 1:33 ; Jer 48:45 fleeing מִכֹּחַ עָֽמְדוּ they stand without strength, Isa 22:3 אֻסָּ֫רוּ מִקֶּשֶׁת (Hi De Di Che) they were bound without the bow (being used) (but Ges as 2e: by the bowmen ), Zeph 3:18 . (On 2Sam 13:16 see We or Dr). See also 7b. with of position , off, on the side of, on , especially with reference to quarters of the heavens (compare πρὸς Νότου , ἐκ δεξιῶν , a fronte, a tergo, etc.): Gen 2:8 ׳י planted a garden in Eden מִקֶּדֶם off, on the east, 12:8 וְהָעַי מִיָּם בֵּיתְאֵל מִקֶּדֶם Bethel off ( on ) the West and `Ai off ( on ) the East; so מִנֶּגֶכ מִצָּפוֺן, מִמִּוְרָח, Josh 11:3 ; 15:8 ; 18:5 ; 1Sam 14:5 , etc.: similarly מִיָּמִין on the right, מִשְּׂמאֹול on the left, מִמּוּל and (more rarely) מִמָּנִים on the front, מֵאָחוֺר = behind ( 2Sam 10:9 ), מִסָּבִיב Deut 12:10 + round about , מִלְמַעְלָה מִמַּעַל, , and מֵעָ֑ל (rare) = above , מִתַּחַת Exod 20:4 + beneath , מִבַּיִת on the inside, מִחוּץ on the outside Gen 6:14 +, מִנֶּגֶד in front, at a distance, 21:16 +, מֵרָחוֺק Exod 2:4 + afar off , מִמְּנִ֫ימָה within , מִזֶּהמִ֗֗֗וֶּה and ֗֗֗ מִמֹּה מִמֹּה on this side . . . on that side. And so even with verbs of motion, as Gen 11:2 בנסעם ויהי מִקֶּדֶם as they journeyed — not from , but — on, the side of the east, virtually = eastwards , 13:11 and Lot journeyed מקדם east , Isa 17:13 ; 22:3 מֵרָחוֺק ברחו they fled — not from afar but — afar , 23:7 whose feet used to carry her מֵרָחוֺק afar off to sojourn, 57:9 thou didst send thy messengers עדמֿרחוק even to afar . With a following לְ (or suffix), most of these words are frequently in the sense of on the east ( west , etc.) of . . ., as Josh 8:13 מִיָּם לָעִיר on the west of the city, לְ מִקֶּדֶם Gen 3:24 , לְ מִצְּפוֺן (construct Ges § 130 a, n .) De); מִן שֹׁנֶה different from Est 1:7 ; 3:8 . b. when an object is compared with a group or multitude of which it forms one, especially with מִכֹּל , Gen 3:1 עָרוּם הַשָּׂדֶה חַיַּת מִכֹּל subtil out of all beasts of the field, or beyond, above all (other) beasts, 3:14 cursed above all cattle (but without implying any judgment whether other cattle are cursed likewise), 37:3 Israel loved Joseph מִכָּלבָּֿנָיו out of all his sons, or above all his (other) sons, Deut 7:7 ; 33:24 אָשֵׁר מִבָּנִים בָּרוּךְ blessed above sons be Asher, Judg 5:24 מִנָּשִׁים תְּבֹרַח blessed above women be Jael, 1Sam 9:2 b 15:33 אִמֶּ֑ךָ מִנָּשִׁים תִּשְׁכַּל כֵּן , 18:30 ; Jer 17:9 מִכֹּל עָקֹב deceitful above all things, Psa 45:3 ; Song 5:10 מֵרְבָבָה דָּגוּל (compare מִן בָּחַר above 2a c: ex in eximius, egregius ; Iliad 18:431 ὅς σ’ , ἐμοὶ ἐκ πάσεων Κρονίδης Ζεὺς ἄλγἐ ἔδωκεν , 3:227 ἔξοχος Ἀργείων . . . κεφαλήν ). c. sometimes in poetry the idea on which מן is logically dependent, is unexpressed, and must be understood by the reader, Isa 10:10 מירושׁלם ופסיליהם and their idols are (more) than (those of) Jerusalem, Micah 7:4 מִמְּסוּכָה יָשָׁר the uprightest is (sharper) than a thorn-hedge (but We from ), Job 11:7 ; 28:18 ; Psa 4:8 מֵעֵת beyond (that of) the time when etc. Ecclesiastes 4:17; Eccl 9:17 ; compare Ezek 15:2 . d. מן not unfrequently expresses the idea of a thing being too much for a person, or surpassing his powers: Gen 18:14 ׳מי הֲיִמָּלֵא דָּבָר can a thing be too hard for J.? (so Deut 17:8 +; compare Psa 131:1 ; 139:6 + ), 32:11 מִן קָטֹנְתִּי , Deut 14:24 הַדֶּרֶךְ מִמְּךָ יִרְבֶּה כִּי = is too great for thee ( 1Kin 19:7 ), 1Ki 32:47 מִכֶּם רֵק : so with עָצַם Gen 26:16 , כָּבֵד be too heavy for Exod 18:18 ; Psa 38:5 , מָךְ Lev 27:8 (too poor to pay), קָשָׁה Deut 1:7 , צַר be too narrow for , 2Kin 6:1 ; Isa 49:19 , קצר 50:2 , אָמַץ Psa 18:18 , נמני ירום is too high for me 61:3 , גָּבַר 65:4 ; מִמְּךָ ַהמְעַט Job 15:11 too little for thee ? מִכֶּם ַהמְעַט Num 16:9 ; Isa 7:13 ; Ezek 34:18 (see מְעַט ; also on 16:20 ); often with an infinitive, as Gen 4:13 מִנְּשׂוֺא עֲוֺנִי גָּדוֺל is greater than I can bear, 30:7 their substance was יַחְדָּו מִשֶּׁבֶת רַב literally great beyond dwelling together = too great for (their) dwelling together, Exod 12:4 ; Judg 7:2 רַב מִתִּתִּי = too great for me to give, 1Sam 25:17 b 1Kin 8:64 מֵהָכִיל רַב , Isa 28:20 ; 33:19 ; 59:1 ; Hab 1:13 ; Psa 40:6 ; Ruth 1:12 : note especially מִן רַב it is more than that . . . (= there is enough of), Exod 9:28 ; 1Kin 12:28 , followed by substantive Ezek 44:6 (see רַב ); and Isa 49:6 וגו לְהָקִים ׳עֶבֶד לִי מִהְיוֺתְךָ נָקֵל too light for thy being my servant was it to raise up, etc., Ezek 8:17 וגו ׳מֵעֲשׂוֺת יִשְׂר לְבֵית ׳הֲנָקֵל was it too trifling to the house of Israel for the doing etc. (less than the doing etc. deserved) ? (but ? read עֲשׂוֺת on analogue of 1Kin 16:31 ). 7 מן is prefixed to an infin.: a. with a causal force (rare), from, on account of, through (compare 2f ): Deut 7:7-8 , י ׳מֵאַהֲבַת אֶתְכֶם through J.'s loving you = because J. loved you, 9:28 (compare 1:27 בְּ ) 2Sam 3:11 אֹתוֺ מִיִּרְאָתוֺ = because he feared him, Isa 48:4 ֗֗֗ מִדַּעְתִּי = because I knew. . . So in מִבִּלְתִּי , ֗֗֗ מִבְּלִי . b. after verbs implying restraint, prevention, cessation , etc., as עֲצָרַנִי מִלֶּדֶת Gen 16:2 hath restrained me from bearing, מִלֶּדֶת וַתַּעֲמֹד 29:35 ; 30:9 : so with חשׂך 20:6 +, חדל + Exod 23:5 +, כִּלָּה + 34:33 +, נִכְלָא 36:6 , מָנַע 1Sam 25:26 +, שׁבת Jer 31:36 +, מֵהַבִּיט יָרֵא Exod 3:6 +, מִןהַֿחֵרֶם שִׁמְרוּ Josh 6:18 ; 2Chr 25:13 מִלֶּכֶת הֵשִׁיב . H4522.fullDef: H4522. mas or mis I. מַס noun masculine 1Ki 5:27 usually collective body of forced labourers, task-workers, labour-band or gang , also (late) forced service, task-work, serfdom ( מִסָּא ᵑ7 , especially in phrase מִיסִּין מַסְּקֵי (implying late and [for Biblical Hebrew] false sense 'tribute,' so Late Hebrew מָסִּים מַעֲלֵי ; √ unknown, probably loan-word; follows analogue of ע׳׳ע ); — absolute ׳מ 1 Kings 5:27 +; לָמַ֑ס Josh 17:13 +; הַמַּ֑ס 2Sam 20:24 +; plural מִסִּים Exod 1:11 ; — 1 labour-band, labour-gang , body of task-workers for public service, formed by levy upon the people by Solomon מִכָּליִֿשְׂרָאֵל מַס שׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ וַיַּ֫עַל 1 Kings 5:27, amounting to 30, 000 men v.1 Kings 5:27; ׳הַמּ הֶעֱלָה אֲשֶׁר 1Kin 9:15 ; עֹבֵד לְמַס שׁ ׳וַיַּעֲלֵם 9:21 and Solomon levied them for a toiling labour-band (compare Gen 49:15 ; Josh 16:10 ) = שׁ וַיַּעֲלֵם ׳לְמַס 2Chr 8:8 ; apparently instituted, earlier, by David, compare עַלהַֿמַּ֑ס וַאֲדֹרָם 2Sam 20:24 , i.e. had charge of the body of labourers, so 1Kin 4:6 ; 1 Kings 5:28; 12:18 2Chr 10:18 . 2. a. of labour-bands, slave-gangs of Israel in Egypt, only מִסִּים שָׂרֵי Exod 1:11 (J) gang-overseers . b. of conquered populations, subject to forced labour: וַעֲבָדוּךָ לָמַס לְךָ יִהְיוּ Deut 20:11 compare Judg 1:30 , 33 , 35 (see GFM), Isa 31:8 ; Lam 1:1 ; so עֹבֵד לְמַס ויהי Josh 16:10 (compare Gen 49:15 ; 1Kin 9:21 ); לָמַ֑ס אֶתהַֿכְּנַעֲנִי וַיִתְּנוּ Josh 17:13 , compare ( וגו ׳וַיָּ֫שֶׂם ) Judg 1:28 . 3 in General: לְמַסעֹֿבֵד וַיְהִי Gen 49:15 and he (Issachar) became a slaving labour-band (poem in J; compare Josh 16:10 ; 1Kin 9:21 ); compare לָמַ֑ס תִּהְיֶה רְמִיָּה Prov 12:24 (here apparently of individual) 4 forced service , serfdom (or possibly (in late passage) tribute = enforced payment , compare Late Hebrew, ᵑ7 , see above), only of Ahasuerus: וגו עַלהָֿאָרֶץ מַס הַמֶּלֶךְ ׳וַיָּשֶׂם Est 10:1 . H4591.fullDef: H4591. maat [ מָעַט ] verb be or become small, diminished, few (Late Hebrew, Talmud, id. ; Arabic is to be without hair on the body ) — Qal Imperfect יִמְעַט Exod 12:4 , 2 masculine plural תִּמְעָ֑טוּ Jer 29:6 , 3 masculine plural יִמְעָ֑טוּ Isa 21:17 +, וַיִּמְעֲטוּ Psa 107:39 ; Infinitive מְעֹט Lev 25:16 ; — Exod 12:4 מִשֶּׂה מִהְיוֺת הַבַּיִת אִסיִֿמְעַט if the house be too small for a lamb; Neh 9:32 כָּלהַֿתְּלָאָה אֵת לְפָנֶיךָ אַליִֿמְעַט (compare Ges § 117l ); of a people, Jer 29:6 וְאַלתִּֿמְעָ֑טוּ שָׁם וּרְבוּ and become not few , 30:19 יִמְעָ֔טוּ וְלֹא וְהִרְבִּתִים , Isa 21:17 ; Psa 107:39 ; Prov 13:11 יִמְעָ֑ט מֵהֶבֶל הוֺן diminishes (opposed to יַרְבֶּה ); Lev 25:16 הַשָּׁנִים מְעֹט וּלְפִי according to the fewness of the years. Pi`el become few (Ges § 52k ), Perfect 3plural Eccl 12:3 מִעֵ֔טוּ כִּי הַטֹּחֲנוֺת וּבָֽטְלוּ . Hiph`il Perfect 3feminine singular consecutive וְהִמְעִ֫יטָה (Ges § 49k ), Lev 26:22 , 1 singular with suffix וְהִמְעַטְתִּים Ezek 29:15 ; Imperfect 2masculine singular תַּמְעִיט Lev 25:16 , תַּמְעִטֵ֫נִי Jeremiah 10:34, 2 feminine singular תַּמְעִ֫יטִי 2Kin 4:3 , etc.; — make small or few, diminish: a. Lev 26:22 (of the sword) אֶתְכֶם וְהִמְעִ֫יטָה , Ezek 29:15 וְהִמְעַטְתִּים , Jer 10:24 תַּמְעִטֵנִי מֶּןֿ אַלבְּֿאַמְּךָ lest thou make me (the people) small , Psa 107:38 יַמְעִיט לֹא וּבְהֶמְתָּם ; Lev 25:16 מִקְנָתוֺ תַּמְעִיט הַשָּׁנִים מְעֹט וּלְפִי according to the smallness (fewness) of the years, thou shalt make small its price, Num 26:54 נַחֲלָתוֺ תַּמְעִיט וְלַמְעַט נַחֲלָתוֺ תַּרְבֶּה לָרַב and to the small (few) thou shalt make small his inheritance (so 33:54 ). b. qualifying an action (sometimes to be understood from the context), Exod 16:17 וְהַמַּמְעִיט הַמַּרְבֶּה וַיִּלְקְטוּ and they gathered, he that made much, and he that made little (that is לִלְקֹט ), 16:18 ; Num 11:32 אסף הממעיט חמרים עשׂרה , 2Kin 4:3 אַלתַּֿמְעִיטִי רֵקִים כֵּלִים empty vessels make not few (that is, in borrowing); Exod 30:15 וגו ׳לָתֵת הַשָּׁ֑קֶל מִמַּחֲצִית יַמְעִיט לֹא וְהַדַּל יַרְבֶּה לֹא הֶעָשִׁיר shall not diminish from the half shekel to give, i.e. shall not give less, Num 35:8 תַּמְעִיטוּ הַמְעַט וּמֵאֵת תַּרְבּוּ הָרַב מֵאֵת and from the few ye shall make few (that is לָתֵת ), i.e. ye shall give few (cities).

H4592.fullDef: H4592. meat מְעַט 101 substantive a little, fewness, a few ; — ׳מ absolute and construct, מְעָ֑ט Isa 10:7 +, plural מְעַטִּים Psa 109:8 ; Eccl 5:1 ; — 1. a. Gen 30:30 לְפָנַי לך היה אשׁר מעט the little that thou hadst, 47:9 חיי שׁני ימי היו ורעים מעט few and evil, Lev 25:52 ; Num 26:54 (compare 33:54 ) נחלתו תמעיט וְלַמְעַט and to the small (few) thou shalt make small his inheritance, 33:56 ; 35:8 תמעיטו ַהמְעַט וּמֵאֵת , Deut 7:7 העמים מכלֿ ַהמְעַט אתם וכי ye are the fewest out of all peoples, 1Sam 14:6 בִמְעָ֑ט אוֺ בְּרַב לְהוֺשִׁיעַ , Jer 42:2 מֵהַרְבֵּה מְעַט נִשְׁאַרְנוּ כִּי we are left as few out of many, Ezek 5:3 בְּמִסְמָּר מְעַט מִשָּׁם וְלָקַחְתָּ , Hag 1:6 מְעָ֑ט וְהָבֵא הַרְבֵּה זְרַעְתֶּם (compare 1:9 ), Psa 8:6 מאלהים מעט ותחסּרהו , 37:16 לַצַּדִּיק מְעַט טוֺב (compare Prov 15:16 ; 16:8 ), 2Chr 29:34 לִמְעָ֑ט הָיוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים רַק ; as predicate Num 13:18 אִםרָֿ֑ב הוּא הַמְעַט , Josh 7:3 הֵמָּה מְעַט כִּי , Job 10:20 ; Ruth 2:7 ; Neh 7:4 ; Isa 16:14 מִזְעָר מְעַט וּשְׁאָר . — Hosea 8:10 מְעַט וַיָּחֵלּוּ and they begin as littleness ( = to be minished ) because of, &c.; but read probably ( ᵐ5 ) מִמְּשֹׁחַ מְעַט וְיֶחְדְּלוּ and they shall cease for a little ( d ) from anointing, etc. b. as substantive with following Genitive, Gen 18:4 מַיִם מְעַט a little of water , 24:17 , 43 , אֹכֶל מְעַט 43:2 ; 44:25 ; 1Sam 14:43 ; 17:28 הָהֵ֫נָּה הַצּאֹן מְעַט literally the fewness of those sheep, Prov 6:10 +; as Genitive to a previous substantive, מְעָ֑ט מְתֵי men of fewness Deut 26:5 ; 28:62 ; in apposition, Isa 10:7 מְעָ֑ט לֹא גּוֺיִם לְהַכְרִית , Ezra 9:8 מְעַט מִחְיָה , Neh 2:12 עִמִּי מְעַט וַאֲנָשִׁים , Eccl 9:4 ; either Genitive or appositive, 10:1 ; Dan 11:34 מְעָ֑ט עֵזֶר יֵעָֽזְרוּ with a help of smallness. c. twice declined as an adjective , Psa 109:8 מְעַטִּים יָמָיו יִהְיוּ , Eccl 5:1 מְעַטִּים דבריך יהיו עלכֿן . d. as adverb. accusative, of place , 2Sam 16:1 מְעַט עֹבֵר וְדָוִד ; of time, Job 10:20 b; of degree, 2Kin 10:18 מְעָ֑ט אֶתהַֿבַּעַל עָבַד אַחְאָב , Ezek 11:16 and have been to them for a sanctuary but little , Zech 1:15 ; repeated מְעַט מְעַט by little, by little = gradually, Exod 23:30 ; Deut 7:22 . e. phrases: — a. with the interr. הֲ , Gen 30:15 וְלָקַחַת אִישִׁי אֶתֿ קַחְתֵּךְ ַהמְעַט was thy taking my husband (too) little? and (wilt thou be) for taking also my son's love-apples? Num 16:9-10 כְּהֻנָּה גַּם וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם ֗֗֗ הִבְדִּיל כִּי מִכֶּם ַהמְעַט is it too little for you that J. hath separated, etc., ... and do ye seek, etc.? 16:13 הִשְׂתָּרֵר גַּם תִשְׂתָּרֵר כִּי ֗֗֗ הֶעֱלִיתָנוּ כִּי ַהמְעַט , Josh 22:17 f. וגו תָּשׁוּבוּ וְאַתֶּם ֗֗֗ לָנוּ ׳ַהמְעַט , Isa 7:13 וגו תַּלְאוּ כִּי אֲנָשִׁים הַלְאוֺת מִכֶּם ׳ַהמְעַט is wearying men too little for you, that you will weary also my God? Ezek 34:18 (as Ew Co AV RV), Job 15:11 אֵל תַּנְחוּמוֺת מִמְּךָ ַהמְעַט . But Ezek 16:20 (si vera lectio) was it (too) little because of thy whoredom? (was that insufficient for thee? Kö iii. 406 m ). b. וְ מְעַט ׳עוֺד , Exod 17:4 וּסְקָלֻנִי מְעַט עוֺד yet a little, and they will stone me, Jer 51:33 ; Hosea 1:4 ; Psa 37:10 ; וְ מִזְעָר מְעַט ׳עוֺד Isa 10:25 ; 29:17 ; compare Hag 2:6 ; Job 24:24 . 2 כִּמְעַט like a little: hence a. within a little, almost (compare ὀλίγου ), Gen 26:10 ֗֗֗ שָׁכַב כִּמְעַט almost had lain ..., Psa 73:2 Qr, 94:17 ; 119:87 ; Prov 5:14 (all followed by perfect); Ezek 16:47 מֵהֶן וַתַּשְׁחִתִי קָט כִּמְעַט like a little , and thou hadst done more corruptly than they; Song 3:4 מֵהֶם שֶׁעָבַרְתִּי כִּמְעַט = hardly had I passed. b. with imperfect, just , 2Sam 19:37 עבדך יעבר כמעט just would thy servant pass over; lightly, easily, quickly (compare δἰ ὀλίγου ), Psa 2:12 אַמּוֺ כִּמְעַט יִבְעַר כִּי , 81:15 ; Job 32:22 . c. = shortly , 2Chr 12:7 . d. = little worth , Prov 10:20 רשׁעים ולב כמעט . e. pleonastic for מְעַט , Isa 1:9 (accents) שָׂרִיר כִּמְעָ֑ט a little remnant, Psa 105:12 (= 1Chr 16:19 ) בָּהּ וְגָרִים כִּמְעַט ; רֶגַע כִּמְעַט like the littleness of a moment = for a little moment, Isa 26:20 ; Ezra 9:8 .

Deut 30:6 ׳ל חַיֶּיךָ for thy life's sake , 1Kin 8:41 the foreigner who comer from afar ׳ל שְׁמֶ֑ךָ , Isa 43:14 בָבֶ֫לָה שִׁלַּחְתִּי לְמַעַנְכֶם , 45:4 ; 62:1 ׳ל ציון , 63:17 ׳ל עבדיך , 65:8 ; Ezek 36:22 (twice in verse); Job 18:4 ; Psa 122:8 ; 122:9 ; ( ד ׳עַבְדִּי ) דָּוִד לְמַעַן , i.e. for the sake of David's memory, and the promises given to him, 1Kin 11:12-13 , 32 , 34 ; 15:4 ; 2Kin 8:19 ; 19:34 (= Isa 37:35 ), 20:6 (all D 2 ); לְמַעֲנִי (of ׳י ) for my own sake , i.e. to vindicate my name, 2Kin 19:34 (= Isa 37:35 ), 2Kin 20:6 ; Isa 43:25 ; 48:11 אֶעֲשֶׁה לְמַעֲנִי לְמַעֲנִי , so לְמַעַנְךָ Dan 9:19 , ׳ל אֲדֹנָי 9:17 ; ׳י is said (or entreated) to act ( שְׁמִי שִׁמְךָ, ) שְׁמוֺ לְמַעַן i.e. to maintain his reputation, or character, Psa 23:3 ; 25:11 ; 31:4 ; 79:9 ; 106:8 ; 143:11 ; Jer 14:7 , 21 ; Ezek 20:9 , 14 , 22 , 44 ; Isa 48:9 ; simile ׳ל חַסְדְּךָ (i.e. to maintain it consistently) Psa 6:5 ; Psalm 44:27, ׳ל טוּבְךָ 25:7 , ׳ל צִדְקוֺ Isa 42:21 . b. In view of, on account of (but not expressing causation distinctly, like מִן 2f , or מִמְּנֵי ), Deut 3:26 י ׳ויתעבר לְמַעַנְכֶם בי on your account , 1Kin 11:39 ׳ל זֹאת in view of this , ׳ל שׁוֺרֲרַי on account of my watchful foes, Psa 5:9 ; 27:11 , ׳ל צורריך 8:3 , simil. 69:19 ; 48:12 ( 97:8 ) ל ֗֗֗ ציון הר ׳ישמח משׁפטיך in view of thy judgments. c. Sq. infinitive Gen 18:19 י הָבִיא ׳לְמַעַן for the purpose of J.'s bringing = to the intent that J. might bring, 37:22 ׳ל הַצִּיל in order to rescue , 50:20 ; Exod 1:11 ; 9:16 ; 10:1 , etc., Deut 2:30 ; Deuteronomy 6:28, etc., 2Kin 10:19 ; Jer 7:10 , 18 ; 11:5 ; 50:34 (on הִרגיע , see עַד 2a b ), Ezek 14:5 ; 21:5 ; 22:6 etc., 36:5 , + often (Kö iii.595 f. ). Once, pleonastic, לֵב לָמוּג לְמַעַן 21:20 (compare לְ כַּעֲבוּר 1Chr 19:3 ; but read probably הִמּוֺג ). 2. conjunction (followed by imperfect): — a. אֲשֶׁר לְמַעַן Gen 18:19 I have known him ׳ל יְצַוֶּה אשׁר to the end that he might command, etc., Deut 27:3 ; Josh 3:4 ; 2Sam 13:5 ; Jer 42:6 ; more often b. without אשׁר , as Gen 12:13 לִי יִיטַב לְמַעַן , 27:25 ; Exod 4:5 ׳ל יאמינו , 8:6 ; 8:18 ; 9:29 ; 10:2 ; Isa 5:19 ; 23:16 ; Psa 9:15 ; Psalm 30:13; 48:14 + often (Kö iii.571 ). c. Sq. לֹא (a) ׳ל לֹא אשׁר Num 17:5 ; Deut 20:18 ; Ezek 31:14 ; 36:30 ; 46:18 ; (b) ׳ל לֹא 14:11 ; 19:9 ; 25:10 ; 26:20 ; Zech 12:7 ; Psa 119:11 ; 119:80 ; 125:3 (Kö iii.574. Less common than לְבִלְתִּי or מִן with infinitive, or מֶּןֿ ). Note 1 — לְמַעַן is always in order that , never merely so that ἐκβατικῶς ); but sometimes, in rhetorical passages, the issue of a line of action, though really undesigned, is represented by it ironically as if it were designed: Deut 29:18 (see Dr) ל ֗֗֗ כִּלְבָבוֺ ׳וְהִתְבָּרֵךְ וגו ׳סְפוֺת and he congratulate himself ... in order to sweep away the moistened with the dry (i.e. to destroy all together), Isa 30:1 ; 44:9 ל ידעו ובל יראו ׳בל יֵבוֺשׁוּ in orer that they may be put to shame, Jer 7:18 ׳ל הַכְעִיסֵנִי , 7:19 ׳ל פְנֵיהֶם בּשֶׁת , 27:10 , 15 ; 32:29 ; Hosea 8:4 their silver, etc., they have made into idols ׳ל יִכָרֵת in order that it may be cut off (of course, not the real purpose of the idolatry), Amos 2:7 ; Micah 6:16 : compare Psa 51:6 (see Comn.) in order that thou mightest be just when thou judgest (that is, by manifesting thy justice in judgement on my sin). compare Qor 28:7 (Fl Kl. Schr. i. 397 f. ). Note 2. — In Josh 4:24 for the anomalous ׳ל יְרָאתֶם , read infinitive ׳ל יִרְאָתָם in order that they might fear (Dr § 14 Obs .): Neh 6:13 אִירָא לְמַעַן הוּא שָׂכוּר לְמַעַן (si vera 1.) the first ׳ל points forwards, to this intent was he hired, to the intent that I should be afraid. — On Prov 16:4 , see מַעֵנֶה above

H5048.definition: or  preposition  in front of, in sight of, opposite to , נֶ֑גֶד , construct נֶגֶד , suffix נֶגְדִּי Psa 38:11 +, נֶגְדְּךָ 38:10 +, etc
H5048.fullDef: H5048. neged נֶ֫גֶד 151 substantive what is conspicuous or in front , always as adverb or preposition in front of, in sight of, opposite to , נֶ֑גֶד , construct נֶגֶד , suffix נֶגְדִּי Psa 38:11 +, נֶגְדְּךָ 38:10 +, etc.; with ה locative נֶ֫גְדָּה 116:14 ; 116:18 ; — 1 as adverb accusative in front of , a. locally (rather stronger and distincter than לִפְנֵי ), ( a ) Gen 31:32 הַכֶּרנָֿא אַחֵינוּ נֶגֶד in front of our brethren own it, now, 31:37 ; 47:15 נגדך נמות ולמה why should we die in thy sight ? Exod 19:2 Israel encamped ההר נגד in front of the mountain, 34:10 נִפְלָאֹת אעשׂה כלעֿמך נגד , before, in sight of, all thy people (compare Psa 78:12 ), Josh 3:16 the people passed over ירחו נגד in front of J., 1Kin 20:27 , etc.; Neh 3:23 in front of their house, 3:29 ; ישׂראל (כלׅ נגד Deut 31:11 ; Josh 8:35 = 1Sam 15:30 ; 2Sam 12:12 +; 1Kin 21:13 set Naboth הָעָם נֶגֶד ; י ׳נגד 1Sam 12:3 ; 16:6 י נֶגֶד ׳אַךְ מְשִׁיחוֺ , so נֶגְדִּי Psa 89:37 , נֶגְדּוֺ 18:13 ; השׁמשׁ נגד Num 25:4 ; 2Sam 12:12 ; Psa 22:26 ׳נ יראיו , Psalm 52:11 (so in poetry לְ נֶגְדָּה 116:14 ; 116:18 ); hostilely, Job 10:17 ; with collateral idea of to the mortification of , Psa 23:5 ; 31:20 , compare Joel 1:16 ; with collateral idea of being open or known to , Prov 15:11 י נגד ואבדון ׳שׁאול , Job 26:6 ; Psa 38:10 כלתֿאותי נגדך || נסתרהׅ לא (ממך , 69:20 (|| יָדַעְתָּ ), 119:168 ; Isa 59:12 ; so הָיוּ מָּנַי נֶגֶד Hosea 7:2 . ( b ) with reflexive suffix, and verb of motion, to go in front of oneself , i.e. straightforward , Josh 6:5 נגדו אישׁ העם ועלו each straightforward , 6:20 ; Amos 4:3 ; Jer 31:29 ; Neh 12:37 , compare Prov 4:25 . b. mentally, = vividly present to , Psa 38:18 תמיד נגדי ומכאובי , 44:16 ; 51:5 תמיד נגדי וחטאתי , 109:15 ׳נ ׳י (remembered by): nearly = נֶגְדּוֺ כְּאַיִן בְּעֵינָיו, Isa 40:17 ; Psa 39:6 ; so נְבוֺנִים מְּנֵיהֶם ׳וְנ Isa 5:21 . But Exod 10:10 פניכם נגד רעה כי before your face is = in your view, or purpose (compare דברבֿליעל עֵינַי לְנֶגֶד אשׁית לא Psa 101:3 ). 2 With prepositions: a. כְּנֶגֶד according to what is in front of = corresponding to , Gen 2:18 I will make him כְּנֶגְדּוֺ עֵזֶר a help corresponding to him i.e. equal and adequate to himself, 2:20 among the animals there was no כְּנֶגְדּוֺ עֵזֶר . **Note that in Late Hebrew מכנגד = in front of , Ber 4:5; 9:5; Ab 2:10, פני מכנגד Git 7:7 and elsewhere. b. לְנֶגֶד in front of, before , Gen 33:12 לְנֶנְדֶּ֑ךָ וְֵאלְכָה , Num 22:32 ; 2Kin 1:13 fell on his knees אליהו לנגד , Isa 1:7 your ground אותהּ אֹכלים זרים לנגדכם ; with עָמַד Josh 5:13 ; Dan 8:15 ; 10:16 , in a hostile sense 10:13 , compare Prov 21:30 ; in the sight or presence of , Hab 1:3 לְנֶגְדִּי וְחָמָס וְשֹׁד , Psa 39:2 לנגדי רשׁע בעוד , 50:8 תמיד לנגדי ועולֹתיך , Nehemiah 3:37; opposite to (probably of opposite choirs), Neh 12:9 , 24 ; = parallel to , 1Chr 5:11 ; = over, for , a business (peculiar) Neh 11:22 ; figurative of what is visible morally, Psa 18:23 לנגדי משׁפטיו כל כי (|| מֶנִּי אָסִיר לֹא ), with to set or place 16:8 ; 54:5 לנגדם אלהים שׂמו לא (compare 86:14 ,), 90:8 ; often in the phrase ֗֗֗ עֵינֵי לְנֶגֶד , both literal, as Job 4:16 ׳לנ עֵינָ֑י תְּמוּנָה , Psa 5:6 לנ הוללים יתיצבו ׳לא עיניך (compare 101:7 ); and in a moral sense, 18:25 לנ ידי ׳כְּבֹר עיניו , 26:3 לנ חסדך ׳כי עיני i.e. is ever present to my mind, 36:2 לנ אלהים פחד ׳אין עיניו i.e. he has no eye to discern God's awe-inspiring judgments (compare 10:5 ); with אשׁית לא i.e. have in view, purpose (|| שׂנאתי ) 101:3 . c. מִנֶּגֶד ( a ) adverb off ( מִן 1c ) the front, in front, opposite, ex adverso , Gen 21:16 מנגד להּ ותשׁב sat her down opposite , 21:16 , 2Kin 2:7 ; Deut 28:66 מנגד לך תלואים חייך והיו shall be hung up for thee in front (i.e. suspended, as by a thread, in front of thee); Judg 9:17 מנגד נפשׁו וישׁלך and flung away his life in front or straight away (i.e. hazarded it); = some way off, from or at a distance , Num 2:2 ; Deut 32:52 הארץ את תראה מִנֶּגֶד כי , 2Kin 2:15 מנ ׳וַיִּרְאֻהוּ at a distance , 3:22 ; 4:25 ; aloof , 2Sam 18:13 מנגד תתיצב ואתה , Obadiah 11 ( b ) as a preposition ( a ) from the front of, away from , Song 6:5 מִנֶּגְדִּי עֵינַיִךְ הָסֵבִּי , 1Sam 26:20 מנ ארצה ׳דמי י ׳פני אליֿפֹל ; עיני מנגד from before the eyes of , with verbs of removing Isa 1:16 , cutting off Psa 31:23 ; Jonah 2:5 , hiding Amos 9:3 ; Jer 16:17 . ( β ) opposite to , Neh 3:19 , 25 , 27 ; at a distance from , Psa 10:5 מנגדו משׁפטיך מרום , 38:12 יעמדו נגעי מנגד . ( γ ) לְ מִנֶּגֶד from before , Prov 14:7 , in front of Judg 20:34 . d. נֶגֶד עַד as far as the front of , Neh 3:16 , 26 .

(rare)); — Qal Perfect ׳נ Zechariah 2:16; 2 masculine singular נָחַלְתָּ Exod 23:20 8 t. H5159.fullDef: H5159. nachalah נַחֲלָה 224 noun feminine possession, property, inheritance (originally gift ; Late Hebrew = Biblical Hebrew); — ׳נ Num 18:23 +; נַחֲלָת Psa 16:6 (Ges § 90g ), read נַחֲלָתִי Ew SS We Kö ii. 1, 425 ; construct נַחֲלַת Josh 13:23 ; suffix נַחֲלָתִי Ruth 4:6 ; נַחֲלַתְכֶם Psa 105:11 ; plural נְחָלוֺת Isa 49:8 , נְחָלֹת Josh 19:51 ; 1 property: a. in Canaan given by ׳י to Israel, ישׂראל נחלת Judg 20:6 ; ׳נ יעקב Isa 58:14 , especially נַחֲלָה לְךָ נֹתֵן אֲשֶׁר Deut 4:21 ; 15:4 ; 19:10 ; 20:16 ; Deuteronomy 21:28; 24:4 ; 25:19 ; 26:1 (all D); עמי את הנחלתי אשׁר הנחלה Jer 12:14 . b. distributive among tribes: נ ׳נתן לְ Num 16:14 ; 36:2 ; Josh 14:3 (restore לְ ), 17:4 , 14 ; 19:49 (all P); לנ ׳נתן לְ Deut 29:7 ; Josh 11:23 ; 14:13 (all D 2 ); נחלה נָָֽחֲלוּ 17:6 (J); בּנ ׳תֵּחָלֵק Num 26:53 , 56 (P); בּנחלה נפל 34:2 (P), Judg 18:1 ; Ezek 47:22 ; בנ ׳הפיל Josh 13:6 ; 23:4 (D 2 ), Ezek 45:1 ; 47:22 , also 47:22 (Co reads ב for מ ). c. nations as possession of the people , Psa 111:6 ; of the king 2:8 . d. Levites have no property in the land Num 18:23-24 , Deut 10:9 ; 12:12 ; their possession is ׳י Num 18:20 (P); ׳י נחלתו הוּא Deut 10:9 ; 18:2 ; Josh 13:14 , 33 (all D); the tithes Num 18:21 , 24 , 26 (P). e. ׳י takes Israel as his property, 1Sam 10:1 ; 1Kin 8:53 ; 2Kin 21:14 ; Isa 19:25 ; Micah 7:18 ; Psa 33:12 ; 68:10 ; 106:5 ; נחלה עם Deut 4:20 (D 2 ); וְנַחֲלָֽתְךָ עַמְּךָ 9:26 , 29 (D), 1Kin 8:51 ; || עַם Isa 47:6 ; Joel 2:17 ; Joel 4:2; Micah 7:14 ; Psa 28:9 ; 78:62 ; 78:71 ; 94:5 ; 94:14 ; 106:40 ; י ׳נחלת 1Sam 26:19 ; 2Sam 20:19 ; 21:3 ; ׳נ אלהים 14:16 ; נ חבל ׳יעקב Deut 32:9 ; נ ׳שׁבט Jer 10:16 = 51:19 , Psa 74:2 ; נ ׳שׁבטי Isa 63:17 ; also, the holy mountain Exod 15:17 (song), temple Jer 12:7 ; Psa 79:1 , land Jer 2:7 ; 12:8-9 , 16:18 ; 50:11 . 2 portion, share: a. assigned by God , Isa 54:17 ; Psa 37:18 ; 127:3 ; elsewhere || חֵלֶק Job 20:29 ; 27:13 ; 31:2 . b. by choice , || נ ׳לא ישׁי בבן לנו חֵלֶק, 2Sam 20:1 we have no share in the son of Jesse = 1Kin 12:16 2Chr 10:16 . 3 inheritance (45 t.) אָבִּינוּ בְּבֵית וְנַחֲלָה חֵלֶק Gen 31:14 (E) portion or inheritance in the house of our father ; נ ׳העביר לְ Num 27:7-8 , (P) cause the inheritance to pass unto ; נ ׳נתן לְ 27:9-10 , 11 (P), Job 42:15 ; אבות נחלת Num 36:3 , 8 ; 1Kin 21:3-4 , Prov 19:14 ; ׳נ תהיה לבניו Ezek 46:16 .

In the phrase מְּנֵי נֹכַח , Jer 17:16 הָיָה מָּנֶיךָ נֹכַח שְׂפָתַי מוֺצָא was before thy face, Lam 2:19 ; Ezek 14:3 מְּנֵיהֶם נֹכַח נָָֽתְנוּ עֲוֺנָם מִכְשׁוֺל (i.e. they contemplate it with pleasure), 14:4 ; 14:7 . 2 combined with prepositions: — a. אֶלנֹֿכַח , Num 19:4 אלנֿ וְהִזָּה ׳מועד אהל פני and sprinkle it towards the front of, etc. b. ׃לְֹנכַח ( a ) as adverb Prov 4:25 לנ ׳עיניך יביטו let thine eyes look to the front or right on (|| נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ יַישִׁרוּ ועפיך ); ( b ) as preposition Gen 30:38 הַצּאֹן לְֹנכַח in front of the flocks 25:21 אִשְׁתּוֺ לְֹנכַח ֗֗֗ וַיֶּעְתַּר in fornt of , i.e. on behalf of (compare pro ), his wife; ( c ) עַדנֹֿכַח , Judg 19:10 עַדנֿ ׳וַיָּבאֹ יְבוּס as fas as in front of Jebus, 20:43 ; Ezek 47:20 ( לְ עַדנֹֿכַח ). Synonym נֶגֶד , q. v.

H5228.fullDef: H5228. nakoach [ נָכֹחַ ] adjective and substantive straight, right, straightness , feminine נְכֹחָה , plural וֺת נְכֹחִים, -: — Isa 57:2 נְכֹחוֺ הֹלֵךְ he that walks in (compare 33:15 ; 50:10 ) his straightness (Ges 'der seinen geraden Weg geht'), figurative for straightforwardly (compare Prov 4:25 ); נְכֹחָה what is straight in front , figurative straightforwardness, honesty , Amos 3:10 נ עֲשׂוֺת יָָֽדְעוּ ׳לֹא , Isa 59:14 ׳ונ לָבוֺא תוּכַל לֹא (|| אֱמֶת ); 2Sam 15:3 וּנְכֹחִים טובים דבריך thy pleadings are good and right (i.e. TRUE ), Prov 8:9 (of words of Wisdom) לַמֵּבִין נְכֹחִים כֻּלָּם i.e. they lead straight to the right goal (|| ישׁרים ; compare 8:8 b וְעִקֵּשׁ נִפָתָּל בָּהֶם אֵין ), 24:26 נְכֹחִים דְּבָרִים מֵשִׁיב i.e. either correct (leading to the right point), or honest answers; Isa 30:10 נְכֹחוֺת לָנוּ לֹאתֶֿחֱזוּ TRUE things (opposed to מַהֲתַלּוֺת חֲלָקוֺת, illusions ), 26:10 יְעַוֵּל נְכֹחוֺת בְּאֶרֶץ in a land of rectitude (Che) he will do wickedly.

H5234.fullDef: H5234. nakar I. [ נָכַר ] verb (not Qal ) regard, recognize (Late Hebrew Hiph`il know, be acquainted with ; ᵑ7 Aph`el id. ; Syriac Aph`el id. ; compare also Arabic in sense be shrewd, cunning ); **Arabic be shrewd , apparently rare, compare cunning Lane 2850a . — Niph`al Perfect 3masculine plural נִכְּרוּ לֹא Lam 4:8 they are not recognized . Pi`el Perfect לִפְנֵידָֿ֑ל שׁוֺע נִכַּר לֹא Job 34:19 he regardeth not the opulent above the poor (|| שָׂרִים מְּנֵי לֹאנָֿשָׂא ); Imperfect תְנַכֵּ֑רוּ לֹא 21:29 do ye not recognize their tokens . Hiph`il Perfect הִכִּיר Deut 33:9 ; Dan 11:39 Kt; suffix הִכִּירוֺ Gen 27:23 ; 3 plural הִכִּירוּ Judg 18:3 2 t., suffix הִכִּירֻהוּ Job 2:12 , הִכִּרֻהוּ Gen 42:8 ; Imperfect יַכִּיר Deut 21:17 3 t. + Dan 11:39 Qr; וַיַּכֵּר Gen 38:26 +; suffix וַיַּכִּרֵ֫הוּ 1Kin 18:7 , יַכִּירֶ֫נּוּ Job 7:10 , וַיַּכִּירָהּ Gen 37:33 , etc.; Imperative ַהכֶּרֿ 31:32 2 t.; Infinitive absolute הֵַכּרֿ (Ginsb van d. H. ַהכֶּרֿ ) Prov 24:23 ; 28:21 ; construct suffix הַכִּירֵנִי Ruth 2:10 ; Participle מַכִּיר Psa 142:5 , suffix מַכִּירֵךְ Ruth 2:19 , etc.; — 1 regard, observe , especially with a view to recognition, with object clause, Gen 31:32 ; 37:32 ; 38:25 ; pay attention to , with accusative of person Ruth 2:10 , 19 ; accusative of thing (of God) Job 34:25 ; accusative of thing omitted 2Sam 3:36 ; ׳י subject לְטוֺבָה ֗֗֗ אַכִּיר כֵּן Jer 24:5 so will I regard the exiles ... for good ; Antiochus subject Dan 11:39 ; מָּנִים הִכִּיר pay regard to (shew partiality, = פ מְּנֵי ׳נָשָׂא ) Deut 1:17 ; 16:19 (|| מִשְׁמָּט הִטָּה ), Prov 24:23 ; 28:21 . 2 Recognize (as formerly known) with accusative of person or thing, Gen 27:23 ; 37:33 ; 38:26 (all J), 42:7-8 , (twice in verse) (E), 1Kin 18:7 ; 20:41 ; Job 2:12 ; proverb. אֶתרֵֿעֵהוּ אִישׁ יַכִּיר בְּטֶרֶם Ruth 3:14 before a man could recognize his fellow (i.e. before dawn); recognize voice ( קוֺל ), Judg 18:3 ; 1Sam 26:17 ; = perceive the true situation, וְהִנֵּה וָאַכִּירָה Neh 6:12 and I perceived, and lo! God had not sent him. 3 Be willing to recognize, acknowledge Deut 21:17 ; 33:9 ; Isa 63:16 (|| יָדַע ), Psa 142:5 ; acknowledge with honour Isa 61:9 . 4 Be acquainted with , מְקוֺמוֺ עוֺד יַכִּירֶנּוּ לֹא Job 7:10 his place shall be acquainted with him no more (he shall be gone and forgotten), compare Psa 103:16 ; with accusative of thing Job 24:17 . 5 Distinguish, understand , לְקוֺל ֗֗֗ קוֺל הִכִּיר Ezra 3:13 could not distinguish , etc.; compare Job 4:16 could not distinguish its appearance ; לְדַבֵּר הִכִּיר Neh 13:24 understand how to speak , etc. Hithpa`el Imperfect יִתְנַכֶּרנָֿ֑עַר Prov 20:11 by his deeds a youth maketh himself known , whether his doing be pure, etc. [ נכר ] verbdenominative act or treat as foreign, or strange; disguise, misconstrue ; — Niph`al Imperfect יִנָּכֵר Prov 26:24 with his lips a hater disguiseth himself (dissembles, speaks what is foreign to his thought). Pi`el Perfect נִכַּר 1Sam 23:7 , but see below; Imperfect וַיְנַכְּרוּ Jer 19:4 and they have treated this place as foreign (profane); צָרֵהוּ יְנַכְּרוּ Deut 32:27 lest their adversaries should misconstrue (it). — א אֹתוֺ ׳נִכַּר בְּיָדִי 1Sam 23:7 God hath alienated him into my hand , but improbable; מָכַר ᵐ5 (compare Judg 4:9 ) hath sold him , so Th Klo HPS (compare We); < סִכַּר (as Isa 19:4 ) Krochm Dr; Kit either of these; > סִגַּר Bu; Löhr either סִגַּר or סִכַּר . Hithpa`el Imperfect אֲלֵיהֶם וַיִּתְנַכֵּר Gen 42:7 he acted as a stranger toward them; Participle feminine מִתְנַכֵּרָ֑ה 1Kin 14:5-6 , feign to be a stranger-woman .

H5236.fullDef: H5236. nekar נֵכָר noun [masculine] that which is foreign, foreignness **(properly unknown , compare Arabic √) (on formation compare Lag BN 51, 154 ); — absolute ׳נ Judg 10:16 +, construct נֵכַרֿ Deut 31:16 ; — foreignness (of another family, tribe, or nation), especially 1 (הַ)נֵּכָר אֱלֹהֵי = foreign gods Gen 35:2 , 4 ; Josh 24:20 , 23 (all E, = ׳א אֲחֵרִים of D, compare אַחֵר ), Judg 10:16 ; 1Sam 7:3 ; Jer 5:19 ; 2Chr 33:5 ; ׳א נֵכַרהָֿאָרֶץ Deut 31:16 = foreign gods of the land ; singular נֵכָר אֵל 32:12 ; Mal 2:11 ; Psa 81:10 ; נ ׳אֱלוֺהַּ Dan 11:39 . 2 בֶּןֿ(הַ)נֵּכָר = foreigner Gen 17:12 (|| מִזַּרְעֲךָ לֹא ), 17:27 ; Exod 12:43 (all P), Lev 22:25 (H), Ezek 44:9 (twice in verse); Neh 9:2 ; Isa 56:3 ; (ה)נ ׳בְּנֵי 2Sam 22:45-46 , = Psa 18:45 ; 18:46 ; Ezek 44:7 ; Isa 56:6 ; 60:10 ; 61:5 ; 62:8 ; Psa 144:7 ; 144:11 . 3 other combinations: נ ׳הַבְלֵי Jer 8:19 foreign vanities (idolatries); הַנּ ׳מִזְבְּחוֺת 2Chr 14:2 foreign altars ; נ ׳אַדְמַת Psa 137:4 foreign soil ; ׳מִכָּלנֿ Neh 13:30 from everything foreign .

H5237.fullDef: H5237. nokri נָכְרִי adjective foreign, alien (Late Hebrew נָכְרִי = Gentile ); — ׳נ absolute masculine Zeph 1:8 +; feminine נָכְרִיָּה Exod 2:22 +; masculine plural נָכְרִים Isa 2:6 2 t. + Prov 20:16 Kt (> Qr נָכְרִיָּה ), + 27:13 (so read for נָכְרִיָּה ᵑ0 ); feminine plural נָכְרִיּוֺת Gen 31:15 +; — 1. a. foreign: נָכְרִי עַם Exod 21:8 (E) a foreign (non-Israel) people, נ ׳אִישׁ Deut 17:15 (|| אָתִיךָ לֹא ); נ ׳מַלְבּוּשׁ Zeph 1:8 ; נָכְרִיָּה אֶרֶץ Exod 2:22 (J) foreign land , so 18:3 (E); especially נָכְרִיּוֺת נָשִׁים foreign (non-Israel) women 1Kin 11:18 ; Ezra 10:2 , 10 , 11 , 14 , 17 , 18 , 44 ; Neh 13:26-27 ,. b. as substantive נָכְרִי foreigner (non-Israel) Judg 19:12 (+ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִבְּנֵי לֹא אֲשֶׁר ), 1Kin 8:41 (+ מֵעַמְּךָ לֹא אֲשֶׁר ), = 2Chr 6:32 (+ id. ), 1Kin 8:43 2Chr 6:33 ; Deut 14:21 (|| גֵּר ), 15:3 ; 23:21 (opposed to אָחִיךָ ), 29:21 (+ רְחוֺקָה מֵאֶרֶץ יָבאֹ אֲשֶׁר ); as predicate, 2Sam 15:19 (|| גֹּלֶה ), נָכְרִיָּה Ruth 2:10 ; plural נָכְרִים foreigners Lam 5:2 ( זָרִים ), Obadiah 11 (|| id. ); compare נָכְרִים יַלְדֵי Isa 2:6 ; feminine plural alien women Gen 31:15 (E; i.e. not of one's father's family). 2 נָכְרִיָּה foreign woman , as technical term, in Proverbs, for harlot (perhaps because harlots were originally chiefly foreigners): Prov 2:16 (|| זָרָה אִשָּׁה ), 7:5 (|| id. ), 5:20 (|| זָרָה ), 6:24 (|| רָ֑ע אֵשֶׁת ), 23:27 (|| זוֺנָה ). — On 20:16 ; 27:13 see below 3 figurative unknown, unfamiliar: בְּעֵינֵיהֶם הָיִיתִי נָכְרִי Job 19:15 an alien am I become in their eyes ; ׳נ אִמִּי לִבְנֵי Psa 69:9 (|| לְאֶחָ֑י הָיִיתִי מוּזָר ); נ ׳אִישׁ Eccl 6:2 ; of ׳י s judgment, עֲבֹדָתוֺ נָכְרִיָּה Isa 28:21 strange is his task! (|| מַעֲשֵׂהוּ זָר ); נָכְרִיָּה גֶּפֶן Jer 2:21 an alien vine (opposed to אֱמֶת זֶרַע ), figurative of degenerate Israel; as substantive, נָכְרִים Prov 20:16 Kt (> Qr נָכְרִיָּה ), alens , persons unknown to him (|| זָר ), so read also (for נָכְרִיָּה ᵑ0 ) || 27:13 .

H5251.fullDef: H5251. nes נֵס noun [masculine] standard, ensign, signal, sign (Late Hebrew id., flag , usually sign , i.e. miracle ; נִסָּא נֵס, ᵑ7 sign, miracle ); — ׳נ absolute Num 21:8 +; construct Isa 11:10 ; suffix נִסִּי Exod 17:15 ; Isa 49:22 ; — 1. a. standard , as rallying-point, ׳י נִסִּי Exod 17:15 (E), ׳י my standard (name of altar); conspicuously set on hill Isa 30:17 (simile of solitariness; || הָהָר עַלרֿאֹשׁ תֹּרֶן ); signal of war [see Schumacher ZPV ix. 232, Across the Jordan, 104 f. ] (especially to the nations, for destruction or deliverance of Judah, Isaiah Jeremiah), נ ׳נָשָׂא לַגּוֺיִם 5:26 ; 11:12 ; compare 18:3 (on mountains, || שׁוֺפָר תָּקַע ); נ ׳אָרִים אֶלעַֿמִּים 49:22 (|| יָדִי אֶלגּֿוֺיִם אֶשָּׂא ), — in all these subject ׳י ; compare עַמִּים לְנֵס עֹמֵד 10:11 (of Messianic king); נ ׳שְׂאוּ 13:2 (on mountain), Jer 50:2 ; 51:12 (with אֶלֿ against ), 51:27 (|| בַּגּוֺיִם שׁוֺפָר תִּקְעוּ ), נ ׳הָרִימוּ עַלעַֿמִּים Isa 62:10 , compare Jer 4:21 (|| שׁוֺפָר קוֺל ); ׳נָתַתָּהנ֗֗֗ לְהִתְנוֺסֵס Psa 60:6 thou hast set a standard (only) for fleeing . b. signal , נ ׳שְׂאוּ צִיּ֫וֺנָה Jer 4:6 (i.e. to direct refugees to Zion). 2 standard , as pole, supporting serpent of bronze Num 21:8-9 , (JE). 3. a. ensign, signal , לְנֵס לָךְ לִהְיוֺת מִפְרָשֵׁךְ הָיָה שֵׁשׁמִ֗֗֗מִּצְרַיִם Ezek 27:7 byssus from Egypt was thy sail, to serve thee for an ensign (so DaToy; on lack of pennon on ancient ships see Co; > strike out Co Berthol); so b. (since sails were the only ensign) = sail Isa 33:23 (Che Di and others; > pennon Ges Hi Ew De Du). 4 sign (compare Late Hebrew) = warning Num 26:10 (P).

H5253.fullDef: H5253. nasag I. [ סוּג , seldom שׂוּג ] verb move away, backslide ( ׳שׂ erroneous; Arabic go and come Lane 1459 , abitus et adventus Frey (Kam)); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular סָג Psa 53:4 ; Imperfect 1plural נָסוֺג 80:19 ; Participle active construct סוּג Prov 14:14 (Ba NB § 124c Ges §§ 50f , 72p); — backslide, prove recreant to ׳י , with מִן Psa 80:19 ; so absolute 53:4 ; לֵב סוּג Prov 14:14 a backslider in heart. Niph`al Perfect 3masculine singular נָסוֺג Psa 44:19 , נָשׂוֺג 2Sam 1:20 ( שׂ for ס ); 1 singular נְסוּגֹּ֫תִי Isa 50:5 ; 3 plural נָסֹ֫גוּ 42:17 ; Jer 38:22 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִסַּג Micah 2:6 (Ges § 72dd , but see below); 3 masculine plural יִמֹּ֫גוּ Psa 35:4 3 t., וַיִּסֹּ֫גוּ 78:57 ; Infinitive absolute נָסוֺג Isa 59:13 ; Participle plural נְסוֺגִים Zeph 1:6 ; Jer 46:5 ; — 1 reflexive turn oneself away, turn back : a. literally of Jonathan's bow 2Sam 1:22 , with מִן (see HPS). b. figurative = prove faithless (as Qal ): (1) of human friends, ׳נס אָחוֺר Jer 38:22 (absolute); usually (2) ׳נס י ׳מֵאַחֲרֵי Zeph 1:6 compare Isa 59:13 ; so absolute Psa 78:57 (+ בָּגַד ), with אָחוֺר Isa 50:5 (|| מָרִיתִי ), Psa 44:19 (|| מִן נָטָה ). — כְּלִמּוֺת יִסַּג לֹא Micah 2:6 could mean reproaches do not depart , i.e. cease (Hi-St Che GASm Now RV); Now proposes also (emending following see) shall not disgrace depart from Jacob's house ? Buhl Lex 13 conjecture, plausibly, יַשִּׂיג (√ נשׂג ) disgrace shall not overtake us . 2 be truned or driven back, be repulsed , of ׳נ s foes: + אָחוֺד Jer 46:5 ; Isa 42:17 ; Psa 35:4 ; 40:15 = 70:3 Psalm 5. Hiph`il 1. usually of displacing, moving back a boundary mark ( גְּבוּ ), Imperfect 2masculine singular תַּסִּיג Deut 19:14 , jussive תַּסֵג Prov 22:10 ; 3 masculine plural יַשִּׂיגוּ Job 24:2 ( שׂ for ס ); Participle ג ׳מַסִּיג Deut 27:17 , ג ׳מַסִּיגֵי Hosea 5:10 . 2 remove carry away , valuables, to rescue them, jussive, 2masculine singular תַּסֵּג Micah 6:14 si vera lectio (on synt.see Dr §§ 152, 1. 2; 155 Obs. ) Hoph`al Perfect 3masculine singular מִשְׁמָּט אָחוֺר וְהֻסַּג Isa 59:14 and justice is driven back (|| תַּעֲמֹד מֵרָחוֺק צְדָקָה ). סוג Ezek 22:18 see following.

H5254.fullDef: H5254. nasah [ נָסָה ] verb Pi`el test, try (Late Hebrew id. , Pi`el; ᵑ7 Pa`el נַסִּי ; Syriac Pa`el ; compare Ethiopic temptation ); — Pi`el Perfect 3masculine singular נִסָּה Deut 4:34 3 t.; suffix נִסָּהוּ Exod 15:25 ; 3 feminine singular נִסְּתָה Deut 28:56 ; 1 singular נִסִּיתִי Eccl 7:23 , + 4 t. Perfect; Imperfect 3masculine singular suffix יְנַסֵּם Dan 1:14 ; 1 singular אֲנַסֶּה Judg 6:39 ; suffix אֲנַסְּכָה Eccl 2:2-3 ;masculine plural יְנַסּוּ Num 14:22 ; 2 masculine plural תְּנַסּ֑וּן Exod 17:2 , + 7 t. Imperfect; Imperative נַס Dan 1:12 ; suffix נַסֵּנִי Psa 26:2 ; Infinitive construct נַסּוֺת Exod 20:20 , + 8 t. Infinitive; Participle מְנַסֶּה Deut 13:4 ; — 1 test, try (synonym בחן ), absolute 1Sam 17:39 (a sword); with בְּ Judges 7:39; Eccl 2:1 ; with accusative Dan 1:12 , 14 ; accusative + בְּ 1Kin 10:1 2Chr 9:1 ; Eccl 7:23 . 2 attempt, assay, try to do a thing, with Infinitive Deut 4:34 ; 28:56 ; with accusative Job 4:2 ( venture a word). 3 test, try, prove, tempt [but not in modern sense of the word: see Dr Deut 6:16 ; Psalms 453, 483] a. God tests or proves Abraham Gen 22:1 (E), Israel Exod 15:25 ; 20:20 (E), 16:4 (J), Deut 8:2 , 16 ; 13:4 ; with בְּ Judg 2:22 ; 3:1 , 4 ; tribe of Levi Deut 33:8 (poem); Hezekiah 2Chr 32:31 ; psalmist Psa 26:2 . b. Israel tests , or tries God: Exod 17:2 , 7 ; Num 14:22 (J), Deut 6:16 ; Psa 78:18 ; 78:41 ; 78:56 ; 95:9 ; 106:14 ; so Ahaz, Isa 7:12 .

H5301.fullDef: H5301. naphach [ נָפַח ] verb breathe, blow ( נפוח כור Ecclus 43:4 a furnace blown upon (heated hot); Late Hebrew נָפַח id. , נְפַח ᵑ7 , Syriac ; Assyrian napâ—u , inflame , nappa—u , smith Dl HWB 474 ; Arabic ( and) blow ; Ethiopic or Di 712 ); — Qal Perfect 3feminine singular נָָֽפְחָה Jer 15:9 ; וְנָפַ֫חְתִּי Hag 1:9 ; וְנָפַחְתִּ֫י Ezek 22:21 ; Imperfect וַיִּמַּח Gen 2:7 ; Imperative feminine singular מְּחִי Ezek 37:9 ; Infinitive (לָ)פַ֫חַת 22:20 ; Perfect active נֹפֵחַ Isa 54:16 ; passive נָפוּחַ Jer 1:13 ; Job 41:12 ; — breathe, blow , חַיִּים נִשְׁמַת בְּאַמּוֺ וַיִּמַּח Gen 2:7 (J); followed by ב also Ezek 37:9 ; Isa 54:16 and Hag 1:9 blow into it (to scatter it); followed by עַלֿ : אֵשׁ עָלָיו לָפַחַת Ezek 22:20 to blow fire upon it (ore, for melting), so figurative 22:21 and I will blow upon you with ( ב ) the fire of my wrath ; ׳נ נַפְשָׁהּ Jer 15:9 she hath breathed out her life (of a mother, compare Hiph`il ); absolute נָפוּחַ סִיר Jer 1:13 a blown (i.e. well-heated, boiling) pot , compare נ ׳דּוּד Job 41:12 (simile). Pu`al Perfect נֻמָּ֑ח לֹא אֵשׁ Job 20:26 a fire not blown (by any human breath). So perhaps also Num 21:30 (reading וגו אֵשׁ ׳עַדנֻֿמַּח until fire was blown [hot] as far as Medeba), compare Di. Hiph`il Perfect 1singular חִמָּ֑חְתִּי בְּעָלֶיהָ נֶפֶשׁ Job 31:39 (or if) the life of its (the land's) owners I have caused them to breathe out ; אוֺתוֺ וְהִמַּחְתֶּם Mal 1:13 and ye have sniffed at it (in contempt).

Lev 27:2 ; construct נַפְשׁוֺת Gen 36:6 4 t.; נַפְשֹׁת Lev 21:11 ; נְפָשִׁים Ezek 13:20 (but read חָפְשִׁים , see Co Berthol Toy); suffix נַפְשׁוֺתָם 2Sam 23:17 +; נַפְשֹׁתָם Num 17:3 +: — 1 = that which breathes, the breathing substance or being = ψυχή , anima, the soul, the inner being of man: a. distinguished from בָּשָׂר וְעַד מִנֶּפֶשׁ ׃בָּשָׂר Isa 10:18 ; הַבָּשָׂר עִם הַנֶּפֶשׁ Deut 12:23 ; from שְׁאֵר Prov 11:17 ; from בֶּטֶן body Psa 31:10 . b. both the inner נפשׁ and the outer בשׂר are conceived as resting on a common substratum: תֶּאֱבָֽל׃ עָלָיו וְנַפְשׁוֺ יִכְאָ֑ב עָלָיו בְּשָׂרוֺ אַךְ Job 14:22 only his flesh upon him is in pain, and his soul upon him mourneth ; compare Psa 42:5 ; 42:7 ; 131:2 ; Job 30:16 ; Lam 3:20 [see עַל 1d ], all poetical (compare 6c ). c. ׳נ departs at death and returns with life: מֵתָה כִּי נַפְשָׁהּ בְּצֵאת וַיְתִי Gen 35:18 (E) and it came to pass when her soul was going forth ( for she died ); נַפְשָׁהּ נָָֽפְחָה Jer 15:9 she breathed out her soul , compare 1Kin 17:21-22 , Job 11:20 ; 31:39 . d. often desired that the נפשׁ may be delivered: from Sh®°ôl Psa 16:10 ; 30:4 ; 49:16 ; 86:13 ; 89:49 ; Prov 23:14 ; from שַׁחַת , the pit of Sh®°ôl , Isa 38:17 ; Job 33:18 , 22 , 28 , 30 . 2 The נפשׁ becomes a living being: by God's breathing חיים נשׁמת into the nostrils of its בשׂר ; of man Gen 2:7 (J); by implication of animals also 2:19 (J); so Psa 104:29 ; 104:30 ; compare 66:9 ; man is חַיָּה נֶפֶשׁ , a living, breathing being Gen 2:7 (J); elsewhere חיּה נפשׁ always of animals 1:20 , 24 , 30 ; 9:12 , 15 , 16 (all P), Ezek 47:9 ; so החיּה נפשׁ Gen 1:21 ; 9:10 (both P), Lev 11:10 , 46 (H); השׁרצת נפשׁ 11:46 (H); חי כל נפשׁ Job 12:10 . נפשׁ is frequently used with the verb ׃חיה נפשׁ וחיתה Gen 12:13 ; 19:20 (both J), 1Kin 20:32 (E), Psa 119:175 ; Jer 38:17 , 20 ; נַפְשְׁךָ חֵי 1Sam 1:26 ; 17:55 ; 20:3 ; 25:26 ; 2Sam 11:11 ; 14:9 ; 2Kin 2:2 , 4 , 6 ; 4:30 (all J E); compare נ ׳יְחַיֶּה 1Kin 20:31 (E), Ezek 18:27 ; Psa 22:30 ; also Gen 19:19 ; Isa 55:3 ; Prov 3:22 . 3 The נפשׁ (without חיה noun or verb) is specified: a. a living being whose life resides in the blood [so in Arabic We Skizzen iii. 217 G. Jacob Arab. Dicht. iv. 9 f. ] (hence sacrificial use of blood, and its prohib. in other uses; first in D), Deut 12:23-24 , only be sure that thou eat not the blood, for the blood is the living being ( הַנֶּפֶשׁ הוּא הַדָּם ); and thou shalt not eat the living being with the flesh ( הַבָּשָׂר עִם הַנֶּפֶשׁ ); thou shalt pour it upon the earth as water ; this is enlarged in H, Lev 17:10-11 , 12 , 14 and in P Gen 9:4-5 , compare Jer 2:34 . b. a serious attack upon the life is an attack upon this inner living being 2Sam 1:9 ; Jer 4:10 ; Jonah 2:6 ; Psa 69:2 ; 124:4 ; 124:5 ; Job 27:3 . c. נפשׁ is used for life itself 171 t., of animals Prov 12:10 , and of man Gen 44:30 (J); נפשׁ תחת נפשׁ life for life Exod 21:23 (E), Lev 24:18 (H), 1Kin 20:39 , 42 ; 2Kin 10:24 ; תחתיכם נפשׁנו Josh 2:14 (J); בנפשׁ נפשׁ Deut 19:21 ; בנפשׁ for the life of 2Sam 14:7 ; Jonah 1:14 ; בכף נפשׁ שׂם put life in one's own hand Judg 12:3 ; 1Sam 19:5 ; 28:21 ; Job 13:14 ; למות נפשׁו חרף Judg 5:18 risked his life to die ; בנפשׁ at the risk of life Num 17:3 (P), 2Sam 23:17 = 1Chr 11:19 (twice in verse), 1Kin 2:23 ; Prov 7:23 ; Lam 5:9 ; נפשׁ בקּשׁ Exod 4:19 (J), 1Sam 20:21 ; 22:23 (twice in verse); 23:15 ; 25:29 ; 2Sam 4:8 ; 16:11 ; 1Kin 19:10 , 14 ; Jer 4:30 ; 11:21 ; 19:7 , 9 ; 21:7 ; 22:25 ; 34:20-21 , 38:16 ; 44:30 (twice in verse); 46:26 ; 49:37 ; Psa 35:4 ; 38:13 ; 40:15 ; 54:5 ; 63:10 ; 70:3 ; 86:14 ; Prov 29:10 ; נ ׳שׁאל 1Kin 3:11 2Chr 1:11 ; 1Kin 19:4 = Jonah 4:8 ; נפשׁ הִכָּה smite mortally Gen 37:21 (J), Deut 19:6 , 11 ; Jer 40:14-15 , נ ׳לקח 1Kin 19:4 ; Jonah 4:3 ; Psa 31:14 ; Prov 1:19 ; מִמָּוֶת נֶפֶשׁ הִצִּיל deliver life from death Josh 2:13 ; Psa 33:19 ; Psalm 56:14; נפשׁ מלּט 1Sam 19:11 ; 2Sam 19:6 (4 t. in verse); 1Kin 1:12 (twice in verse); Jer 48:6 ; 51:6 , 45 ; Ezek 33:5 ; Amos 2:14-15 , Psa 89:49 ; 116:4 ; ׳נ פדה 2Sam 4:9 ; 1Kin 1:29 ; Psalm 34:23; Psa 49:16 ; 55:19 ; 71:23 ; נ ׳שׁמר 25:20 ; 97:10 ; Job 2:6 ; Prov 13:3 ; 16:17 ; 19:16 ; 22:5 . 4 The נפשׁ as the essential of man stands for the man himself: a. paraphrase for personal pronoun especially in poetry and ornate discourse, 70 t.; (1) נַפְשִׁי = me: נפשׁי תבא אל Gen 49:6 let me not enter (poem in J); נ ׳תָּמֹת ישׁרים מות Num 23:10 let me die , etc. (poem); נַפְשְׁי תָּמוֺת Judg 16:30 (J); נפשׁי אמרה Lam 3:24 I say . (2) נַפְשְׁךָ = thee: נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ תַּחַת לְאֻמִּים Isa 43:4 peoples instead of thee ; לְנַפְשֵׁךְ אָֽמְרוּ 51:23 . (3) נַפְשׁוֺ = he: תלין בטוב נפשׁו Psalms he will not dwell in good circumstances . (4) נַפְשֵׁנוּ = we: יוֺקְשִׁים מִמַּח נִמְלְטָה כְּצִמּוֺר נַפְשֵׁנוּ Psa 124:7 . (5) נַפְשָׁם = they, them: הָלָ֑כָה בַּשְּׁבִי נַפְשָׁם Isa 46:2 they are gone into captivity ; לנפשׁם אוי 3:9 . b. = reflexive, self , 53 t.: נפשׁ על אסר bind oneself Num 30:3 ; 30:5 (twice in verse); 30:6 ; 30:7 ; 30:8 ; 30:9 ; 30:10 ; 30:11 ; 30:12 ; נ ׳לְעַנֹּת 30:14 to afflict oneself . (1) נַפְשִׁי = myself: נפשׁי אדע לא Job 9:21 I know not myself . (2) נַפְשְׁךָ = thyself: נ ׳שׁמר Deut 4:9 keep thyself . (3) נַפְשׁוֺ = himself: כנ ׳אהב 1Sam 18:1 , 3 ; 20:17 loved as himself . (4) נַפְשָׁהּ = herself: נ ׳צדּקה Jer 3:11 justified herself . (5) נַפְשָׁם = themselves: נ ׳הציל deliver themselves Isa 47:14 ; Ezek 14:14 , 20 . (6) נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם נַפְשְׁכֶם, = yourselves: נ ׳אַלתַּֿשִּׁאוּ Jer 37:9 deceive not yourselves , also 42:20 ; 44:7 ; נ ׳ענּה Lev 16:29 , 31 ; 23:27 , 32 ; Num 29:7 (P); לנ ׳נשׁמרתם Deut 4:15 ; Josh 23:11 (D). (7) נַפְשׁוֺתֵינוּ = ourselves: נ ׳על Jer 26:19 against ourselves . c. = person of man, individual, 144 t., first in D 2 ; especially in H, P, and kindred writers: (1) with אָדָם : ׳נ אדם Lev 24:17 opposed to ׳נ בהמה 24:18 (both H), and so ׳נ אדם human persons Num 31:35 , 40 , 46 (P) 1Chr 5:21 ; Ezek 27:13 . Elsewhere without אדם : ׳נ ברכה Prov 11:25 one who blesses ; ׳נ רְמִיָּה 19:15 idle person ; ׳נ נ ׳תחת person in place of person , Job 16:4 ; נ ׳על כמּר Exod 30:15-16 , Num 15:28 ; 31:50 (all P) Lev 17:11 (H). (2) נפשׁ = person, any one: Deut 24:7 ; 27:25 ; Prov 28:17 ; Ezek 18:4 (3 t. in verse); 33:6 ; elsewhere only H P: Lev 2:1 ; 4:2 , 27 ; 5:1-2 , 4 , 15 , 17 ; Leviticus 5:21; 7:18 , 20 , 21 , 25 , 27 ; 23:29-30 , (twice in verse); Num 5:6 ; 15:27 , 30 ; 19:22 ; 31:19 , 28 ; 35:11 , 15 , 30 (twice in verse); Josh 20:3 , 9 (all P), Lev 17:10 , 12 , 15 ; 20:6 (twice in verse); 22:6 , 11 (all H); מן הַהִוא הנ ׳נכרתה that person shall be cut off from: only in Gen 17:14 ; Exod 12:15 , 19 ; 31:14 ; Lev 7:20-21 , 27 ; Num 9:13 ; 15:30-31 , 19:13 , 20 (all P), Lev 19:8 ; 22:3 (both H). (3) נפשׁ collective for persons , in enumerations: Deut 10:22 ; Josh 10:28 , 30 , 32 , 35 , 37 (twice in verse); 10:39 ; 11:11 (all D 2 ) Jer 43:6 ; 52:29-30 , (twice in verse); Ezek 22:25 ; elsewhere only Gen 12:5 ; 46:15 , 18 , 22 , 25 , 26 (twice in verse); 46:27 (twice in verse); Exod 1:5 (twice in verse); 12:16 ; Num 31:35 , 40 (all P). (4) נְפָשׁוֺת persons Gen 36:6 ; Exod 12:4 ; 16:16 ; Num 19:18 (all P), Lev 18:29 ; 20:25 ; 27:2 (all H), 2Kin 12:5 ; Prov 11:30 ; 14:25 ; Ezek 13:18 (3 t. in verse); 13:19 (twice in verse); 13:20 (twice in verse); 17:17 ; 18:4 ; 22:27 ( נפשׁים 13:20 see above). (5) נפשׁ = deceased person , sometimes with מֵת נֶפֶשׁ מֵת, Num 6:6 (P), מֵת נַפְשֹׁת ( נֶפֶשׁ ᵑ6 ᵐ5 ) Lev 21:11 (H); usually without (ה)אדם נפשׁ מֵת, Num 9:6-7 , 19:11 , 13 (P); or simply נפשׁ , Lev 19:28 ; 21:1 ; 22:4 (all H) Num 5:2 ; 6:11 ; 9:10 (all P); elsewhere only Hag 2:13 . 5 נפשׁ = seat of the appetites , in all periods (46 t.) — a. hunger: ׳נ רְעֵבָה hungry soul Psa 107:9 ; Prov 27:7 ; with noun or verb of שׂבע satisfy Isa 56:11 ; 58:10 ; Jer 50:19 ; Ezek 7:19 ; Psa 63:6 ; 107:9 ; Prov 13:25 ; 27:7 ; לנ ׳מתוק 16:24 sweet to the taste . b. thirst: ׳נ עֲיֵפָה weary soul Prov 25:25 ; Jer 31:25 ; ׳נ עיפה כארץ Psa 143:6 ; נ ׳צמאה 42:3 ; 63:2 . c. appetite in General: בנ ׳אֹיְבַי עָלָיו יַקִּיפוּ Psa 17:9 my enemies compass me about with greed ; פִיהָ וּפָֽעֲרָה נַפְשָׁהּ שְׁאוֺל הִרְחִיבָה Isa 5:14 Sh®°ôl enlarged her appetite , etc., compare Hab 2:5 ; Prov 23:2 נֶפֶשׁ בַּעַל ; Ecclesiastes uses נפשׁ only in the sense of a, b, c ; the נפשׁ craves, lacks, and is filled with good things: Eccl 2:24 ; 4:8 ; 6:2-3 , 7 , 9 ; 7:28 . 6 = ׳נ seat of emotions and passions (151 t.) — a. desire: נ ׳אִוְּתָה soul desires Deut 12:20 ; 14:26 ; 1Sam 2:16 ; 2Sam 3:21 ; 1Kin 11:37 ; Job 23:13 ; Prov 13:4 ; 21:10 ; Micah 7:1 ; נ ׳תַּאֲוַת Psa 10:3 ; Isa 26:8 ; נ ׳אַוַּת Deut 12:15 , 20 , 21 ; 18:6 ; 1Sam 23:20 ; Jer 2:24 ; so also לנפשׁ according to one's desire Deut 21:14 ; Psa 78:18 ; Jer 34:16 ; כנפשׁ Deut 23:25 ; נפשׁנו האח ah, our desire Psa 35:25 ; בנפשׁ at one's desire 105:22 ; Ezek 16:27 ; בְדַבְּרוֺ ׳נ יָָֽצְאָה Song 5:6 ; נ ׳נשׂא lift up the soul, desire Deut 24:15 ; 2Sam 14:14 (read אליהם , not אלהים ), Psa 24:4 ; 25:1 ; 86:4 ; 143:8 ; Prov 19:8 ; Jer 22:27 ; 44:14 ; Hosea 4:8 . b. abhorrence, loathing: נ ׳געלה soul abhorreth Lev 26:11 , 15 , 30 , 43 (H) Jer 14:19 ; נ ׳וגם בי בחלה Zech 11:8 and their soul also fell a loathing against me . c. sorrow and distress: נ ׳מרי bitter, gloomy, discontented of soul Judg 18:25 (E) 2Sam 17:8 ; Job 3:20 ; Prov 31:6 ; נ ׳מר 1Sam 22:2 compare Job 7:11 ; 10:1 ; Isa 38:15 ; Ezek 27:1 ; נ ׳עָֽגְמָה Job 30:35 grieved ; נ ׳אגמי sad of soul Isa 19:10 ; נ ׳תבכה my soul shall weep Jer 13:17 ; ׳נ ירעה his soul trembleth Isa 15:4 ; נ ׳צרת distress of soul Gen 42:21 (E). d. joy: ׳נ תגיל my soul rejoiceth Psa 35:9 ; Isa 61:10 ; נ ׳שׂמּח rejoice the soul Psa 86:4 ; also 94:19 ; 138:3 ; Prov 29:17 . e. love: נ ׳אהבה my soul loveth Song 1:7 ; 3:1-2 , 3 , 4 ; נ ׳יְדִדוּת darling of my soul Jer 12:7 ; נ ׳דבקה ׳ב his soul clave unto Gen 34:3 (J), with אחרי Psa 63:9 ; ׳נ ׳ב חשׁקה soul is attached to Gen 34:8 (P). f. alienation, hatred, revenge: נ ׳תֵּקַע מן the soul is alienated from Jer 6:8 ; Ezek 23:17-18 , נ ׳נקעה מן 23:18 , 22 , 28 ; נ ׳שְׂנֻאי hated of soul 2Sam 5:8 (Qr); נ ׳שׂנאה Psa 11:5 ; Isa 1:14 . g. other emotions and feelings: נ ׳השׁיב bring back soul Lam 1:11 , 19 (i.e. revive, compare with שׁוּב 1Kin 17:21 f.), hence figurative refresh, cheer , 17:16 ; Psa 19:8 ; Prov 25:14 ; Ruth 4:15 ; נ ׳שׁובב Psa 23:3 ; נ ׳מַחְמַל your souls' compassion Ezek 24:21 ; נ ׳קצרה soul was impatient Num 21:4 (E), Judg 10:16 ; 16:16 ; Zech 11:8 ; נ ׳אאריך כי that I should prolong my patience Job 6:11 אתנֿ ׳ידעתם הגר ye know the feeling of the stranger Exod 23:9 (R D ). 7 נפשׁ is used occasionally for mental acts + לבב (see 10 ); possibly also alone, owing to unconscious assimilation by late writers; but most, if not all, examples may be otherwise explained: מאד ידעת נפשׁי Psa 139:14 my soul knoweth well (or I know well ; compare 4a ); נ ׳דעת טוב לא בלא Prov 19:2 that the soul be without knowledge is not good (but RVm desire without knowledge , compare 6a ); לנ חכמה ׳דעה 24:14 know wisdom for thy soul (or according to thy desire , compare 6a ); בנ תדמי ׳אל Est 4:13 think not in thy soul (or in thyself , compare 4b ); ׳בג שׁער כמו Prov 23:7 as he reckoneth in his soul (but RV in himself , compare 4b ); נ תאמר ׳מה 1Sam 20:4 (but AV RV following ᵐ5 ἐπιθυμεῖ = תְּאַוֶּה ; see 6a ). 8 נפשׁ for acts of the will is dubious: נפשׁכם ישׁ אם ( את ) if it is your purpose Gen 23:8 (P) 2Kin 9:15 (or if it is your desire , 6a ); נ ׳בחרה my soul chooseth Job 7:15 ; נ ׳מאנה my soul, refuseth 6:7 ; Psa 77:3 ; ׳נ חפצה their soul delighteth in Isa 66:3 ; ׳נ רצתה my soul delighteth in 42:1 ; (all perhaps emotional, 6b, d, g ). 9 נפשׁ = character is still more dubious: נ ׳לאֹיָָֽֿשְׁרָה בּוֺ Hab 2:4 his soul is not right in him (but ᵐ5 οὐκ εὐδοκεῖ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐν αὐτῷ [ εὐδοκεῖ = רצתה ], see 6 ); מְטֻמָּאָה לאֹ נַפְשִׁי Ezek 4:14 my soul hath not (or I have not , 4a ) been polluted. 10 ׳נ in D, when used with לבב , is assimilated to it, and shares with it the meanings of 7, 8, 9 ; and so in later writers influenced by D (unless we may think that ׳ל is used of intellect, while ׳נ is used of the feelings): thus, נפשׁ ובכל לבב בכל (see לבב ): with דרשׁ Deut 4:29 ; 2Chr 15:12 ; עשׂה Deut 26:16 ; אהב 6:5 ; 13:4 ; 30:6 ; ידע Josh 23:14 ; עבד Deut 10:12 ; 11:13 ; Josh 22:5 ; בקלו שׁמע Deut 30:2 ; אל שׁוב 30:10 ; 1Kin 8:48 2Chr 6:38 ; 2Kin 23:25 ; מצות שׁמר 23:3 2Chr 34:31 ; לפני הלך 1Kin 2:4 ; and Deut 11:18 ; 1Sam 2:35 ; 1Chr 22:19 ; 28:9 ; Jer 32:41 ; Psalm 13:8; Prov 2:10 ; 24:12 . Note. — In three cases is Generally found closer approach to supposed radical meaning breath: — a. נפשׁ מעצת רעהו ומתק לב ישׂמח וקטרת שׁמן Prov 27:9 . Ges (after Döderlein) renders a. נ ׳מעצת more than odorous trees , so later edds., even Buhl; but ᵑ9 De SS transpose) נ ׳וּמֶתֶק רֵעֵהוּ מֵעֲצַת . ᵐ5 Hi Bi ומתקרעה = the soul is rent asunder by cares . In any case נפשׁ is || לב , compare 10. b. תְּלַהֵט גֶּחָלִים נַפְשׁוֺ Job 41:13 his breath kindleth coals (of the crocodile).The piece is one of the latest in the book; primitive meaning hardly in such a passage; context favours reference to passion or fury ; perhaps below 6f , his passion or fury kindleth coals. c. הַנֶּפֶשׁ בָּתֵּי Isa 3:20 perfume boxes ; meaning evident from context; but not necessarily scent (breath)-boxes ; may be 6a , boxes of desire , or 5 , boxes exciting the sense of smell; = smelling boxes or bottles. No sufficient evidence in Biblical Hebrew, therefore, for meaning breath, odour . — See, for complete study of נֶפֶשׁ (all passages), Br JBL 1897, 17 ff .

H5329.definition: be pre-eminent, enduring (Ecclus [Pi`el] make brilliant Ecclesiasticus 43:5
H5329.fullDef: H5329. natsach I. [ נָצַח ] verb be pre-eminent, enduring (Ecclus [Pi`el] make brilliant Ecclesiasticus 43:5; Ecclesiasticus 43:13 [?] (compare Oxford ed. xxxiii ); Late Hebrew נָצַח conquer , etc.; Phoenician נצח , Aramaic נְצַח , shine, be illustrious, pre-eminent, victorious ; Arabic be pure, reliable ; Ethiopic be pure, innocent ; both classes of meaning probably derived form shine, be bright, brilliant , see also Dr 1Sam 15:29 ); — Niph`al Participle active feminine נִצַּ֫חַת Jer 8:5 enduring ( מְשֻׁבָה apostasy ). Piel = act as overseer, superintendent, director , only Chronicles and Psalm-titles; — Infinitive לְנַצֵּחַ 1Chr 15:21 4 t.; participle לַמְנַצֵּחַ Hab 3:19 ; Psa 4:1 54t. Psalms; plural מְנַצְּחִים 2Chr 2:1 ; 2:17 ; 34:13 ; — 1 in building temple 2Chr 2:1 ; 2:17 ; Ezra 3:8-9 , compare 2Chr 34:12-13 ,. 2 in ministry of house of ׳י 1Chr 23:4 . 3 in liturgical service of song, עלהֿשׁמינית , over the bass voices, leading them with כִּנֹּרוֺת 1Chr 15:21 ; לַמְנַצֵּחַ in titles Psalms has probably simile meaning, = musical director or choirmaster ; Greek Vrss. of 2nd cent. A.D., Aq Theod Sym, and so Jerome, think of Aramaic victorious , but no clear explanation; ᵐ5 εἰς τὸ τέλος (probably לַמִּנְצָח ) follows ordinary meaning of noun נֵצַח , which may be explained in eschatological sense as referring to end of age of world after Euseb Theod; or for full rendering after De; neither satisfactory. Chronicles, near in date, gives the clue which is intrinsically probably: לְ indicates, not assignment (nothing special in these Psalms to suggest it, and assignment of Psalms for such use a matter of course), but that these Psalms were taken by final editor from an older major Psalter known as the Director's Collection, compare the still earlier collections known as קרח (ל)בני (ל)אסף, (ל)דוד, . The 55 Psalms with למנצח were taken 39 from Davidic, 9 from Korahite, and 5 from Asaphic Psalters; only 2anonymous. Habakkuk 3 originally belonged to Director's Psalter. This and other Director's Psalms have musical directions in titles. The Director's Psalter was probably the prayer-book of synagogue of Greek period, presupposed by our Hab., the collection of the twelve Minor Prophets, the prophetic canon, and Daniel (see Br Gen. Intr. 123 ). [ נְצַח ] verb Hithpa. distinguish oneself (see Biblical Hebrew I. נצח ); — Participle מִתְנַצַּח Dan 6:4 , עַל person

H5378.fullDef: H5378. nasha I. Hiph`il Imperfect 3masculine singular בּוֺ אוֺיֵב לֹאיַֿשִּׁיא Psa 89:23 an enemy shall not act the creditor against him, make exactions of him (|| יְעַנֶּנּוּ ). — 1Kin 8:31 ; 2Chr 6:22 see נשׂא Qal 1 b (5). I. נָשָׁה verb lend, become a creditor (compare I. נשׁא ); — Qal Perfect 1singular נָשִׁ֫יתִי Jer 15:10 ; 3 plural נָשׁוּ 15:10 ; Participle נשֶׁה Exod 22:24 4 t.; plural נשִׁים Neh 5:10-11 , + 5:7 Qr (Kt נשְׁאִים , see I. נשׁא ), suffix נוֺשַׁי Isa 50:1 ; — lend , usually with ב person: וְלֹאנָֿשׁוּבִֿי לֹאנָֿשִׁיתִי Jer 15:10 I have not lent, and they have not lent to me , Deut 24:11 ; Neh 5:7 (Qr; + accusative of congnate meaning with verb), 5:10 ; 5:11 (both + accusative of thing); participle as substantive creditor, usurer Exod 22:24 (E), 2Kin 4:1 ; Isa 24:2 ; 50:1 ; Psa 109:11 .
