H9008.definition: (Biblical Aramaic and הֲ ᵑ7 , Arabic ), prefixed, as a rule, to the first word of a sentence (or clause)
H9008.fullDef: הֶ הַּ , הַ, הֲ, (on the different forms, see Ges § 100 . 4: on Deut 32:6 , see הַל ), interrogative particle (Biblical Aramaic and הֲ ᵑ7 , Arabic ), prefixed, as a rule, to the first word of a sentence (or clause). 1 in direct questions: a. as a simple interrogative , where the answer expected is uncertain, Exod 2:7 הַאֵלֵךְ shall I go and call thee a nurse ? 1Sam 23:11 הֲיַסְגִּרֻנִי will the men of Keilah deliver me into his hand ? שָׁאוּל הֲיֵרֵד will Saul come down ? Job 1:8 ; and frequently. b. often in questions, expressed in a tone of surprise, or put rhetorically , to which a negative answer is expected (= Latin num ? ): Gen 4:9 אָנֹכִי אָחִי הֲשֹׁמֵר Amos I my brother's keeper ? 18:17 shall I hide from Abraham that which I am about to do ? 30:2 ; 50:19 ; Num 11:23 a Deut 4:33 עַם֗֗֗ הֲשָׁמַע Did a people ever hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire, . . . and live ? 20:19 (read with ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵑ7 ᵐ5 Ew Ke Di etc. הֶאָדָם for הָאָדָם ), 2Sam 7:5 בַיִת תִּבְנֶהלִּֿי ַהאַתָּה (altered in 1Chr 17:4 to the negative וג תִּבְנֶה אַתָּה ׳לֹא ), 2Kin 6:22 ֗֗֗ שָׁבִיתָ הַאֲשֶׁר those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow, wilt thou smite ? Isa 28:24 ; 36:12 ; a 57:6 ; 58:5 ; Jer 15:12 ; 16:20 ; Amos 5:25 ; Psa 50:13 ; Job 8:11 ; 15:7-8 , 11 ; 38:12 , 16 , 17 , 22 etc.; before an infinitive absolute (Ew § 328 a ) Jer 7:9 ; Job 40:2 and probably Micah 2:7 (read הֶאָמוֺר : ). After a protasis, הִנֵההֲ֗֗֗ Num 22:38 ; 2Kin 7:2 , 19 ; Jer 32:27 ; Ezek 17:10 ; after הֵן Jer 3:1 ; Hag 2:12 : compare after זוּלַי Gen 24:5 ; after אִם Job 14:14 הֲיִחְיֶה גֶּבֶר יָמוּת אִם a man dieth, shall he live ? Occasionally, one or more words precede הֲ (in the same clause) for special emphasis: 2Sam 7:7 ; Job 34:31 הֶאָמַר אֶלאֵֿל כִּי for to God did one ever say. . .. Neh 13:27 ; Jer 22:15 ( הֲלֹא ), compare 23:26 . c. it is used in questions which, by seeming to make doubtful what cannot be denied, have the force of an impassioned or indignant affirmation : Gen 27:36 ('dubitantis speciem prae se fert Esavus, ut eo acerbius affirmet,' Maurer, cited by Ges), 1Sam 2:27 וגי נִגְלֵיתִי הֲנִגְלהֹ Did I reveal myself to the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt ? etc. (i.e. of course I did, although thy sons, by their actions, appear to belie it), 1Kin 16:31 (expressing astonishment), 21:19 וְגַםיָֿרָ֑שְׁתָּ הֲרָצַחְתָּ Hast thou slain, and also taken possession ? Jer 31:20 ; Job 20:4 ; 41:1 (compare Hi); also Gen 16:13 , and the phrases הַרְּאִיתֶם do ye see ? 1Sam 10:24 ; 2Kin 6:32 ; הֲרָאִיתָ dost thou see ? 1Kin 20:13 ; Ezek 8:12 , 15 , 17 and elsewhere d. in disjunctive questions , the first question being introduced usually by הֲ , the second by אִם or (more rarely) וְאִם : see examples under אִם 2 (p. 50). The disjunctive question may express a real alternative (as Josh 5:13 ), or (as especially in poetry) the same thought may be repeated in a different form, in two parallel clauses (e.g. Isa 10:15 ): in the latter case, the answer No is usually expected. Only very rarely is the second question introduced by הֲ Judg 14:15 (where, however, הֲלֹם ought no doubt to be read, with MSS., ᵑ7 Be and others, for הֲלֹא ), or אוֺ 18:19 ; Job 16:3 ; 38:28 , 31 . 2 In indirect interrogation, whether (German ob . . . .?) — a. singly, after verbs of seeing Gen 8:8 הֲ לִרְאוֺת to see whether , 18:21 ; Exod 4:18 ; Song 6:11 , telling Gen 43:6 , trying Deut 13:4 , knowing Judg 3:4 ; Eccl 3:21 (read הַעֹלָה and הֲיֹרֶדֶת : see De or Wr on the passage .) b. disjunctively, — usually אִם ֗֗֗ הֲ , Num 13:18 end, 13:19 a (and see the land) ֗֗֗ רָעָה אִם הִיא הֲטוֺבָה whether it be good or bad, 13:19 b; 13:20 ; 13:20 ; לֹא אִם ֗֗֗ הֲ Gen 24:21 ; 27:21 ; 37:32 ; Exod 16:4 that I may try it (the people) לֹא אִם בְּתוֺרָתִי הֲיֵלֵךְ whether it will walk in my law or not, Num 11:23 ; Deut 8:2 ; Judg 2:22 ; הֲ ֗֗֗ הֲ Num 13:18 (by side of אִם ֗֗֗ הֲ ); אוֺ ֗֗֗ הֲ Eccl 2:19 ; 11:6 . It is prefixed to other particles, as הֲלֹא הֲכִי, הֲגַם, הַאַף, הַאִם, : see אַף אִם, ,etc. p. 49, etc.
